papers.title: CD19 CAR T cell therapy reshapes the host microbiota immune axis in autoimmune diseases
papers.authors: Zaiss, M. M.; Maeda, Y.; Yi-Yuan, L.; Redanz, S.; Petrov, V.; Gimaev, I.; Fehringer, M.; Pereira, M. S.; Robeck, S.; Chu, J.; Hagen, M.; Wirsching, A.; Rothe, T.; Prinzensteiner, M.; Bozec, A.; Mueller, F.; Mackensen, A.; Vogl, T.; Schett, G.; Brito, I. L.; Kriegel, M. A.
papers.abstract: CD19 targeted CAR T cell therapy induces profound B cell depletion and clinical responses in autoimmune disease; however, whether it reshapes host microbiota interactions remains unknown. We longitudinally profiled gut microbiome composition and microbiota-specific humoral immunity in 20 patients with systemic lupus erythematosus, systemic sclerosis, or idiopathic inflammatory myopathy undergoing CAR T cell therapy, alongside 23 healthy controls, using shotgun metagenomics, IgA/IgG-bound microbiota profiling, and PhIP Seq. CAR T cell therapy reshaped microbiota directed humoral immunity, with reduced fecal IgA and serum anti commensal IgA and IgG accompanied by selective remodeling of microbiota-reactive antibody repertoires. This finding was paralleled by selective changes in gut microbial composition, including depletion of Bifidobacterium adolescentis, without uniform depletion of disease-associated pathobionts. Integrated host microbiome analyses identified altered predicted protein protein interactions involving the immunoproteasome and B cell plasma cell pathways, with interactions before CAR T cell intervention being significantly associated with subsequent relapse. Consistent with these findings, taxon specific IgA targeting, but not global diversity of IgA IgG coated microbiota, differed according to subsequent relapse. Lower baseline fecal IgA was also associated with delayed B-cell reconstitution, linking mucosal humoral immunity to immune recovery after CAR T cell therapy.

papers.title: TREM2 + Macrophages Promote Immune Evasion in Endometriosis Through BAG3-Associated Regulation of CD8 + T Cell Autophagy.
papers.authors: Yuan M, Jiao X, Xu L, Ren Q, Wang S, Zhong Z, Li N, Li Q, Meng X, Wang G.
papers.abstract: Macrophages are the most abundant immune cells in endometriotic lesions, but the roles of specific macrophage subsets in local immune dysfunction remain poorly understood. Here, combining single-cell RNA sequencing of 11 clinical samples with TREM2 knockout mouse models, co-culture experiments, and pharmacological intervention, we identify TREM2 + macrophages as an immunoregulatory population enriched in endometriosis. CD8 + T and natural killer (NK) cells in endometriotic lesions exhibited exhaustion-associated features and reduced cytotoxicity. Cell-cell communication analysis and functional experiments revealed that TREM2 + macrophages regulated CD8 + T cell activity through SPP1-CD44-associated communication and BAG3-associated autophagy regulation. In a mouse model of endometriosis, TREM2 deficiency enhanced CD8 + T and NK cell cytotoxicity and reduced ectopic lesion growth. Pharmacological disruption of the BAG3-HSP70 interaction with YM-1 impaired CD8 + T cell function and promoted lesion growth, and BAG3 silencing reduced autophagy-related markers and effector function in CD8 + T cells, supporting the involvement of BAG3-associated regulation in TREM2 + macrophage-mediated immune dysfunction. Our data identify TREM2 + macrophages as important regulators of immune dysregulation in endometriosis and highlight TREM2 as a potential target for future non-hormonal therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: METTL1-mediated tRNA m7G methylome remodeling drives macrophage M2 polarization and paclitaxel resistance in cervical cancer.
papers.authors: Yi H, Han Y, Wang X, Li Q, Xiong L, Li S.
papers.abstract: Objective Chemoresistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment of cervical cancer. Emerging evidence suggests that RNA methylation plays a crucial role in shaping tumor-immune interactions. However, the role of METTL1-mediated tRNA m7G modification in macrophage polarization and drug resistance is largely unexplored. Methods Functional effects of METTL1 were examined through gain- and loss-of-function experiments in vitro , and xenograft models. Trac-seq was performed to characterize tRNA m7G remodeling. Result METTL1 was significantly upregulated in cervical cancer tissues and was predominantly expressed in macrophages within paclitaxel-resistant tumor samples. METTL1 overexpression promoted M2-like macrophage polarization, whereas METTL1 knockdown produced the opposite effects. METTL1-overexpressing macrophages enhanced cervical cancer cell proliferation and attenuated paclitaxel-induced cytotoxicity in vitro and promoted tumor growth under paclitaxel treatment in vivo . Trac-seq revealed extensive remodeling of tRNA m7G methylome following METTL1 overexpression, with selective hypo- and hypermethylation across distinct tRNAs. Single-cell analysis identified reduced NLRP3 expression in METTL1-high macrophages, and METTL1 overexpression suppressed pyroptosis, whereas WDR4 depletion produced opposing effects and partially attenuated METTL1-mediated changes in macrophages. Conclusion METTL1 promotes M2-like macrophage polarization and paclitaxel resistance in cervical cancer, accompanied by extensive remodeling of the tRNA m7G methylome, providing a potential epitranscriptomic link between macrophage reprogramming and chemoresistance.

papers.title: A quantitative molecular model of the lymphocyte death timer
papers.authors: Ruhle, M.; Thomas, E.; Dann, E.; Gottscheber, N.; Teh, C. E.; Gray, D. H.; Dowling, M. R.; Heinzel, S.; Hodgkin, P. D.
papers.abstract: When stimulated, individual lymphocytes program times for division and death that are inherited within families, revealing a common timing mechanism transmitted over generations. Here we describe a threshold-based mechanism for the time to die. By comparing protein levels in control and apoptosis disabled B and T lymphocytes, we show that death can be predicted by a cooperating ensemble of BCL-2 family proteins falling below a critical threshold. Single cell measurements predict the time of death with a simple formula, where additional inhibition factors explain accelerated death induced by BH3 mimetic compounds. Thus, we identify the death timer as a protein-threshold device that underlies signal integration machinery. Together these results reveal that predicting lymphocyte behavior at single cell level, in complex environments, is possible with modular models that incorporate independent timers and heritability features of critical proteins.

papers.title: A viral replication level-dependent continuum of transcriptional and microRNA reprogramming in HIV-1-infected microglia links productive infection to neurocognitive-associated gene networks.
papers.authors: Vahdat Z, Sharma S, Truong K, Koirala A, Rankothgedera S, Thevasagayampillai S, Kandasamy A, Grimm SL, Zhou S, Gunaratne PH, Kimata JT, Walss-Bass C, Coarfa C, Rice AP.
papers.abstract: Microglia are major targets of HIV-1 in the brain. Despite effective antiviral therapy, infected microglia, including those containing a replication-defective provirus, can express viral products that contribute to neuroinflammation, yet how productive infection shapes the host response remains poorly defined. Using single-cell RNA-seq of HIV-1-infected C20 microglia, we stratified cells by HIV-1 splice junction-supporting reads into low- and high-infection groups, resolving a graded rather than binary host transcriptional response. The computational pipeline developed for this quantification is made publicly available. A core set of immune and cell cycle pathways was induced, regardless of infection level, but several programs reversed direction with increasing viral burden: interferon-α/γ and EMT /hypoxia signatures peaked at low infection, while high infection featured suppression of these signatures alongside induction of mTORC1 / MYC signaling, ribosome biogenesis, RNA processing, and mitotic activity, with progressive loss of cytoskeletal, motility, and developmental programs. This pattern, except for cell cycle/mitotic signatures, was reproduced in iPSC-derived microglia, supporting its generalizability beyond an immortalized cell line. To identify potential regulatory mechanisms underlying these transcriptional programs, we integrated differentially expressed miRNAs and genes from the low- and high-infection groups, filtered for the canonical inverse miRNA-target relationship, revealing miRNA/mRNA networks enriched for miRNAs previously implicated in HIV-1 replication (e.g., miR-33a-5p and miR-3065-3p ) and in neurodegenerative and psychiatric disease (e.g., miR-107 and let-7c-5p ). These findings define a productive infection-level continuum in microglial transcription and miRNA reprogramming and identify candidate miRNA-mediated mechanisms, complementary to the canonical Env / Nef / Tat pathway by which HIV-1-infected microglia may contribute to neuroinflammation and neurocognitive impairment in people with HIV-1.IMPORTANCEHIV-1 persists in the brain despite antiviral therapy in part because infected microglia continue to express viral RNA and proteins that promote neuroinflammation, contributing to the cognitive impairment seen in many people with HIV-1. How the level of active viral replication within a microglial cell shapes its response has been unclear since most infection models capture only an averaged, post-replication snapshot rather than the transition from low to advanced infection. By ranking microglia by HIV-1 splice junction-supporting reads, we show that the host transcriptional response is graded rather than binary, and that several pathways, including interferon and growth/proliferative signaling, reverse direction as viral load increases. We further identify a network of HIV-1-dysregulated miRNAs, several previously linked to viral replication or to neurodegenerative and neurocognitive disease, pointing to a mechanism by which infected microglia may influence neuronal health, complementary to the well-studied viral Env , Nef , and Tat proteins.

papers.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Inflammation in Prodromal Parkinson's Disease
papers.authors: Yasumizu, Y.; Deerhake, M. E.; Corbin-Stein, N. J.; Neish, K. J.; Moon, J.; Buitrago-Pocasangre, N.; Renkl, E.; Esposito, S.; Russo, A.; Wang, H.; Zhu, B.; Seibyl, J. P.; Reddy, V.; Cheon, M.; Wang, Q.; Spillantini, M. G.; Posner, D. A.; Sumida, T. S.; Longbrake, E. E.; Clatworthy, M.; Cedarbaum, J. M.; Zhang, L.; Hafler, D. A.
papers.abstract: We hypothesized that prodromal Parkinson's disease (PD), characterized by rapid eye movement sleep behavior disorder (RBD) and/or hyposmia, begins with inflammation in the central nervous system that evolves into neurodegeneration. We combined clinical phenotyping and proteomics with single-cell RNA sequencing of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and blood from individuals with RBD, PD, and healthy controls, with multiple sclerosis as a comparator. CSF immune cell numbers were increased in RBD, particularly in those with lower prodromal PD probability scores, a composite score associated with time to phenoconversion. In these participants, CSF macrophages showed enhanced TNF, IL-6/JAK/STAT3, and interferon-{gamma} signaling and predicted crosstalk with CD4+ T cells involving TNF, antigen presentation, and costimulatory pathways. CSF Macrophages resembled mouse dural macrophages and shared TNF signaling with gut immune cells from -synuclein mouse models. These findings uncover a stage-specific TNF-associated inflammation involving crosstalk between CSF Macrophages and CD4+ T cells in prodromal PD.

papers.title: Ketogenic Fasting Suppresses Tumor Growth and Enhances PD-1 Blockade Efficacy Through Glutamine Partitioning and Microbial Metabolite Remodeling.
papers.authors: Xiao M, Wan AH, Lin R, Zhang H, You N, Liang H, Liu C, Zheng Y, Yan S, Zhang Z, Jiang D, Chen M, Cheng H, Zou Z, Fang J, Neumann S, Wang N, Wang QP, Wang Z, Zhang X, Wan G.
papers.abstract: Many tumors remain poorly responsive to immune checkpoint blockade. The metabolic microenvironment in tumors can mediate immunosuppression by failing to sustain productive cytotoxic lymphocyte function. Here, we showed that a coordinated ketogenic-fasting (KF) regimen sensitized immune-refractory tumors to PD-1 blockade by integrating distinct metabolic and microbial effects of ketogenic diet (KD) and intermittent fasting (IF). The KF combination established a distinct immunometabolic state that could not be fully recapitulated by either KD or IF intervention alone. KF induced systemic glucose restriction while preserving intratumoral glutamine availability and selectively upregulating the glutamine transporters SLC38A1 and SLC38A2 in tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells and NK cells, fueling interferon-STAT1 signaling and effector activity. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis identified KF-associated cytotoxic lymphocyte states characterized by enhanced nutrient access signatures, increased effector function, and reduced terminal dysfunction. Microbiota depletion attenuated KF-mediated tumor control without abolishing intratumoral glutamine enrichment. Fecal microbiota transfer and monocolonization identified Odoribacter splanchnicus as sufficient to restore tumor control and cytotoxic T-cell activity in microbiota-depleted hosts. Mechanistically, O. splanchnicus was linked to host polyamine remodeling and indole-3-lactic acid, which supported durable CD8+ T-cell functions distinct from the glutamine-driven effector arm. KF enhanced anti-PD-1 efficacy in immune-cold tumor models, and public human datasets showed concordant associations between glutamine context, Odoribacter abundance, and immunotherapy response. Together, these findings identify a diet-responsive host-microbiota metabolic mechanism that stimulates antitumor immunity and sensitizes immune-cold tumors to immunotherapy.

papers.title: Shared Molecular Signatures and Pathways in Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder, Schizophrenia, and Bipolar Disorder: An Integrative Transcriptomic and Machine-Learning Study
papers.authors: Khan, M.; ISLAM, M. A.; Hossain, M. A.
papers.abstract: Abstract Objective: Psychiatric disorders such as post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder (BD) are complex conditions with overlapping molecular features that remain poorly understood. This study aimed to identify shared molecular abnormalities and potential therapeutic targets associated with these disorders. Methods: RStudio (version 4.4.1) was used to process and analyze gene expression datasets from the NCBI database to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). FunRich, DAVID, STRING, and NetworkAnalyst were used for gene ontology and pathway enrichment, protein-protein interaction analysis, transcription factor and microRNA regulatory network analysis, and protein-chemical interaction analysis. The discriminatory ability of prioritized hub genes and transcription factors was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Four machine-learning algorithms (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM-RBF, and Gradient Boosting) were compared using leave-one-out cross-validation on the GSE403628 dataset, comprising 14 controls and 14 cases. Results: Among 32 common genes, several candidate hub proteins were identified, including HLA-DRA, HLA-A, HLA-B, HLA-DOB, and BRD2. The analysis also identified transcription factors (FOXC1, NFYA, RELA, GATA2, FOXL1, SRF, and NFIC), miRNAs (hsa-mir-129-2-3p, hsa-mir-148b-3p, hsa-mir-196a-5p, hsa-mir-26a-5p, hsa-mir-27a-3p, hsa-mir-23b-3p, hsa-mir-500a-3p, hsa-mir-423-5p, hsa-miR-142-5p, and hsa-miR-671-5p), and chemicals, including estradiol, antirheumatic agents, and valproic acid. ROC analysis showed the highest AUC for HLA-DRA (0.760) among hub genes and FOXC1 (0.658) among transcription factors. The hub-gene set consistently outperformed the transcription-factor set across all four machine-learning algorithms, with Logistic Regression achieving the highest AUC (0.800). Random Forest and SVM-RBF achieved the highest accuracy (0.679) under leave-one-out cross-validation. Conclusion: This computational approach identified potential biomarkers linking PTSD, schizophrenia, and BD to immune-related and infectious disease pathways. ROC and machine-learning analyses highlighted HLA-DRA as a promising discriminator between disease and control samples, providing candidate molecular targets for further investigation.

papers.title: Comprehensive Immunoprofiling and Multi-Omics Modeling Reveal Key Immune Features Associated with Disease Progression and Clinical Outcomes in Patients with Unresectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma.
papers.authors: Yang Z, Wu Y, Ji X, Chen Y, Chen X, Wang W, Wen W, Mu W, Ge Y.
papers.abstract: Comprehensive profiling of peripheral immune cells has shown prognostic and disease-monitoring value across multiple cancers, but its clinical relevance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), particularly unresectable HCC, remains insufficiently defined. To address this gap, we performed integrated peripheral immunoprofiling combining T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire sequencing, flow cytometry-based T-cell phenotyping, bulk RNA sequencing, and public single-cell RNA-seq analysis in healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients. This design enabled characterization of HCC-associated and stage-associated peripheral immune alterations and identification of immunotherapy-relevant features in unresectable HCC. Single-cell analysis and flow cytometry revealed remodeling of circulating T-cell states in unresectable HCC, including reduced naïve-like compartments, enrichment of Treg-like cells, and increased memory/effector differentiation. TCR repertoire analysis showed reduced diversity, increased clonal dominance, altered V-J gene usage, decreased interindividual sharing, and convergent motif-level alterations, with early CD4 + TCR perturbations in resectable HCC and more pronounced CD8 + repertoire restriction in unresectable disease. Exploratory GLIPH-based motif analysis, HLA inference, and peptide-HLA binding prediction suggested candidate motif-HLA antigen associations involving hepatitis virus-derived antigens and recurrent HCC mutation-derived candidate neoantigens, although experimental validation is required. Bulk RNA-seq of peripheral CD8 + T cells revealed higher Activation/Effector function, Exhaustion, and Anergy signature scores in both resectable and unresectable HCC than in HDs, with no significant differences between the two HCC groups, whereas the Chemokine/Chemokine receptor signature was specifically increased in unresectable HCC. The overall IFN-response signature did not differ significantly among the three groups. Integrative machine-learning models were then developed using 818 peripheral immune-related features. Among them, the random forest (RF) model effectively distinguished healthy donors, resectable HCC patients, and unresectable HCC patients, with consistently high sensitivity and area under the curve (AUC) in both cross-validation and an independent validation cohort. In unresectable HCC patients receiving immunotherapy, four features derived from TCR-seq and T-cell subset profiling discriminated responders (CR/PR) from non-responders (SD/PD) in univariate analyses, while multivariate prioritization further highlighted ULBP1 as a consistently prioritized response-associated feature that requires validation in an independent cohort. Overall, this study supports comprehensive peripheral immune profiling as an exploratory framework for identifying stage-associated immune alterations and candidate biomarkers to inform personalized immunotherapy strategies in HCC.

papers.title: Early fate bias and TCR sequence shape CD8+ T cell differentiation and expansion.
papers.authors: Brown RJ, Chen Y, Lin S, Shen J, Kasmani MY, Attanasio J, de Menezes MN, Khatun A, Zhu A, Parish IA, Joshi NS, Zamora AE, Cui W.
papers.abstract: When a naive CD8+ T cell encounters an antigen, it proliferates into descendants with identical T cell receptors (TCRs), termed clones. Whether their differentiation toward effector or memory fates is stochastic or TCR-dependent has remained unclear, largely because the vast diversity of TCRs makes individual clones difficult to trace over time. Using single-cell RNA and TCR sequencing in acute LCMV Armstrong infection, we found that clonal distributions in blood reflect those in lymphoid organs, enabling nonlethal longitudinal tracking of clonal evolution. Tracing hundreds of clones, we found that memory clonal distribution is surprisingly uncoupled from early dominance; instead, early central memory precursor frequency predicts memory dominance. Leveraging convergent recombination, we identified clones with identical CDR3 amino acid sequences in mice and found that these natural biological replicates were more likely than chance to adopt similar fates, although substantial clone-to-clone variation remained. Applying the TCR distance algorithm, we further identified dominant motifs associated with enhanced expansion and effector-biased transcriptional programs, extending the TCR's role in shaping clonal differentiation.

papers.title: CD8⁺ T Cell Immune Signatures Bridging Systemic Inflammation and Coronary Artery Injury in Kawasaki Disease.
papers.authors: Chen J, Zhang Y, Wang D, Li K, Liu Z, Wang Y, Lu Z, Qian G, Liu P, Zhang M, Li J, Lv H, Wang S.
papers.abstract: Kawasaki disease (KD) is an acute onset, childhood systemic vasculitis with the most important complication being coronary artery injury with aneurysm formation. In the pathogenesis of KD, innate immune overactivation is well recognized, but the role of adaptive immunity in the progression of vascular lesions is not completely understood. A local lesion in the coronary artery is thought to connect to the systemic inflammatory reaction through CD8 + T cells. In this review, we discuss evidence from peripheral blood immunophenotyping, single cell transcriptomics, TCR clonal repertoire profiling, human coronary artery pathology and KD like animal models to delineate CD8⁺ T-cell signatures and their proposed pathogenic mechanisms. The circulating CD8 + T cells from acute-phase patients have decreased numbers, increased activation markers, skewed subset distribution, and co-existent proliferative and CTL and exhaustion phenotype transcription profiles in conjunction with TCR clonal expansion. CD8 + T cells appear to infiltrate the coronary arterial lesions in human autopsy samples and CD8 + T cells induce coronary arteritis in murine models. Interestingly, classical perforin-granzyme-mediated cytotoxicity of lesional CD8 + T cells is not confirmed in human KD, underscoring a crucial gap between peripheral omics signatures, data in animal models and evidence in human tissues. The in situ effector mechanisms of disease driving CD8+ T cells subsets, and their feasibility as clinical biomarkers, warrant further investigation and may lead to precision risk stratification and targeted immunotherapies in KD related vascular complications, using multicenter prospective cohorts and paired blood and tissue functional assays.

papers.title: Regulatory T cells in kidney diseases: context-dependent functions and therapeutic potential.
papers.authors: Liu L, Chen Y, Liu L, Xie J, Zheng SG.
papers.abstract: Kidney diseases, including acute kidney injury (AKI), chronic kidney disease (CKD), IgA nephropathy (IgAN), lupus nephritis (LN), and kidney transplantation, share features of immune dysregulation, persistent inflammation, and progressive fibrosis. Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are central to immune tolerance in the kidney, yet their function is not uniform: it is shaped by developmental origin, disease etiology, disease stage and the metabolic and inflammatory tone of the renal microenvironment. Single-cell and spatially resolved profiling has revealed tissue-resident, activated, dysfunctional, and senescent Treg states in the injured kidney, and has begun to define the renal Treg niche. Building on this evidence, we propose an etiology- and stage-stratified framework in which Tregs protect against acute injury, promote repair, or, under specific conditions, contribute to fibrotic remodeling. This framework rationalizes therapeutic targeting: cytokine and small-molecule Treg expansion (notably low-dose IL-2), Treg-compatible optimization of conventional immunosuppression, adoptive polyclonal and antigen-specific CAR/TCR-Treg therapies, and metabolic or tissue-targeted engineering should be matched to disease etiology and stage. Integrating spatial multi-omics, lineage-stabilizing strategies, and standardized manufacturing and monitoring will be essential to translate Treg-based therapies into precision treatments for kidney diseases.

papers.title: Distinct T cell subsets associated with responses to different neoadjuvant treatments in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Song XY, Liu ZC, Hu HH, Li Y, Lin L, Yang Y, Li HX, Feng W, Zhang Q, Cai XW, Liu J, Yu W, Li ZG, Fu XL.
papers.abstract: The optimal integration of immunotherapy with chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in neoadjuvant treatment of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) remains unclear. We integrate paired pre- and post-treatment single-cell RNA sequencing and TCR sequencing data from patients receiving neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy (NICT), chemoradiotherapy (NCRT), or immuno-chemoradiotherapy (NICRT) to investigate how these regimens shape intratumoral CD8 + T cell responses. Favorable responses to NICT are associated with maintenance of pre-existing CXCL13 + PD-1 + CD8 + T cells and post-treatment enrichment of a progenitor-like CD8Tex_CXCR4 subset. In contrast, CRT responders show reduced CXCL13 + CD8 + T cells and enrichment of clonally expanded, cytotoxic PD-1 - CD8Teff_NIBAN1 cells. These divergent programs are validated in public datasets and independent prospective cohorts. In murine models, radiotherapy limits PD-1 + T cell expansion, whereas induction anti-PD-1 treatment followed by radiotherapy improves tumor control. Together, these findings reveal distinct CD8 + T cell programs associated with response to different neoadjuvant modalities and provide a cellular rationale for optimizing immunotherapy-radiotherapy sequencing.

papers.title: Multiple Sclerosis Relapses Are Associated With EBV-Specific T-Cell Expansion Amid Broad Immune Activation.
papers.authors: Adda L, Vantomme H, Mhanna V, Stys P, Barennes P, Jouannet C, Coatnoan N, Diderot V, Dubois J, Louapre C, Rosenzwajg M, Mariotti-Ferrandiz E, Klatzmann D.
papers.abstract: Background and objectives Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infection is strongly implicated in multiple sclerosis (MS), yet the mechanisms linking EBV to disease pathogenesis remain unclear. EBV-specific T cells are hypothesized to contribute to MS through molecular mimicry. We aimed to investigate the relationship between EBV-specific T cells and MS relapses using longitudinal T-cell receptor (TCR) repertoire profiling. Methods We analyzed TCR repertoires from sequential peripheral blood samples collected before and after relapses in 5 patients with MS. CD4 + and CD8 + T cells were sorted into naive, memory, and regulatory subsets. TCR antigen specificity was determined using exact matches to public databases and GLIPH2-based clustering, covering EBV, cytomegalovirus, influenza, Mycobacterium tuberculosis , and self-antigens. The results were compared with those from healthy controls. Results At baseline, patients with MS showed a significant enrichment of EBV-specific TCRs within CD8 + T cells, comparable with patterns seen in other autoimmune diseases. After relapses, EBV-specific TCR frequencies markedly increased across all T-cell subsets. TCRs recognizing other viral antigens, including polyspecific TCRs with broad reactivity, displayed similar baseline enrichment and relapse-associated expansion patterns. Discussion Our findings indicate a temporal association between MS relapses, global immune activation, and EBV-specific T-cell expansions, which is consistent with a two-step model of MS relapse immunopathogenesis. An initial, unidentified trigger induces broad immune activation, promoting the expansion of antiviral T cells, including those specific to EBV. These EBV-specific and polyspecific T cells with heightened cross-reactivity may then contribute to MS relapses. Larger studies are needed to further define the role of T-cell dynamics in MS pathogenesis.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk Transcriptomic Profiling of Urothelial Carcinoma: Immunotherapy Associations and Functional Characterization of LY6E.
papers.authors: Huang Y, Zhang C, Xie X, Miao X, Quan Z.
papers.abstract: Background Translating single-cell immune profiles into bulk transcriptomic biomarkers requires distinguishing cell-state signals from overall immune abundance. We evaluated the recovery and clinical relevance of single-cell-derived immune modules in urothelial carcinoma and investigated LY6E as a candidate for functional follow-up. Methods We analyzed 73,279 single cells from two GSE223971 preparations, with eight matched CD45-enriched single-cell/bulk pairs and six broader preparation pairs from five patients. Immune modules underwent donor-support filtering, patient-level validation, lineage adjustment, and comparison with reference-profile methods. Clinical associations were assessed in GSE176307 and IMvigor210, with repeated cross-validation used to evaluate incremental prediction in IMvigor210. An expression-based screen followed by clinical and immune-context assessment prioritized LY6E for knockdown and rescue experiments in 5637 and J82 cells. Results Thirteen of 39 annotated states met donor-support criteria. Four modules passed the initial transfer screen, although all four 95% bootstrap intervals included zero; none of 11 testable subtypes met the within-lineage specificity criteria. Plasma alone passed the cross-preparation module screen (patient-level Spearman rho = 0.900; exact p = 0.083), with weaker recovery by ProM (rho = 0.700). Its association with complete response versus progressive disease in the selected IMvigor210 subset attenuated after immune adjustment, and adding Plasma yielded no consistent predictive improvement. Several immune scores were associated with survival in unadjusted GSE176307 models without supported objective-response associations. LY6E was upregulated in TCGA-BLCA and GSE13507 tumors, but its associations with immunotherapy outcomes differed between cohorts. Two shRNAs reduced LY6E transcript abundance by 64%-67%, decreased growth and migration, and increased apoptosis in both cell lines. An shRNA-resistant construct restored LY6E expression and clonogenic growth. Conclusions Single-cell and bulk transcriptomic integration recovered a Plasma-related abundance signal without establishing subtype specificity or independent immunotherapy prediction. LY6E supported growth and survival in the tested bladder cancer cell lines, whereas its relevance as an immunotherapy biomarker remains unestablished.

papers.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses reveal ferro-aging-related molecular characteristics and immunological heterogeneity in renal cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Xu Y, Zhuang Y, Fang Q.
papers.abstract: Objective Ferro-aging, characterized by chronic iron-dependent oxidative damage and age-related transcriptional alterations, may contribute to the heterogeneity of renal cell carcinoma (RCC). This study aimed to identify ferro-aging-related candidate core genes and evaluate their diagnostic value and biological relevance in RCC. Methods GSE40435 and GSE66272 were integrated as the training cohort, and GSE53757 was used for external validation. Ferro-aging-related candidate genes were identified by differential expression and machine-learning analyses to construct a diagnostic model. Their biological relevance was investigated using immune, molecular subtype, WGCNA, single-cell, and virtual knockout analyses, followed by experimental validation of gene expression and LOX function. Results A total of 26 ferro-aging-related differentially expressed genes were identified, from which five candidate core genes-DPEP1, LCN2, LOX, NOX4, and TLR4-were selected. The five-gene diagnostic model showed strong discriminatory performance, with AUCs of 0.952 and 0.978 in the training and independent validation cohorts, respectively. These genes were associated with immune-related and molecular features and exhibited heterogeneous cell-type-resolved expression patterns, with the combined five-gene signature showing relatively higher module scores in the epithelial/tumor epithelial compartment. Virtual knockout identified NNMT and FAM134B as potential common response nodes. LOX knockdown significantly inhibited RCC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion and increased lipid peroxidation. Conclusion DPEP1, LCN2, LOX, NOX4, and TLR4 represent potential ferro-aging-related diagnostic biomarkers in RCC. LOX may be associated with RCC progression and ferro-aging-related lipid peroxidation, although the underlying mechanisms require further investigation.

papers.title: Predictive factors for TKI discontinuation eligibility and treatment-free remission in chronic myeloid leukemia.
papers.authors: Ono T.
papers.abstract: Treatment-free remission (TFR) is an important therapeutic goal in chronic-phase chronic myeloid leukemia. However, not all patients achieve tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) discontinuation eligibility (TDE), and approximately half of those who discontinue therapy experience molecular recurrence. Thus, achieving TDE and maintaining TFR represent related but distinct clinical challenges. Early molecular response kinetics, treatment duration, depth and stability of response, prior TKI resistance, and BCR::ABL1 transcript type have been associated with these outcomes. Emerging biomarkers, including highly sensitive methods, leukemic stem cell characteristics, clonal hematopoiesis, immune-cell profiles, inflammatory cytokines, and host immunogenetic factors, may further refine prediction. Transcriptomic studies, artificial intelligence-based analysis, and mathematical modeling also offer promising approaches for integrating disease biology, host immunity, and treatment dynamics. Whether predictors identified with conventional TKIs apply to asciminib requires further evaluation. Future strategies should integrate longitudinal molecular and biological information to enable safer and appropriately timed TKI discontinuation.

papers.title: Immune evasion in cancer dormancy and metastatic reactivation.
papers.authors: Gejman RS, Ling HH, Efe G, Luthria K, Shah P, Izar B.
papers.abstract: Metastatic dormancy reflects a dynamic immune-tumor equilibrium in which disseminated tumor cells, either as individual cells or multicellular ecosystems, may persist for years before relapse. Recent studies show that dormant cells evade elimination through spatial and numerical rarity, insufficient immune effectors, suppression of innate immune signaling and inflammasome pathways, and adaptation to local immune niches. Inflammatory stress leading to tissue remodeling dampens immune restraint and promotes metastatic outgrowth. Emerging spatial and single-cell genomic and evolutionary profiling approaches now offer a potential path toward defining dormant disseminated tumor cell states and niches directly in patients. Here, we review mechanisms of tumor-immune interactions in dormant cells or incipient metastases and discuss how these could be leveraged to develop strategies to eradicate minimal residual disease, restore immune surveillance, and prevent inflammatory reawakening. We also provide a perspective on how predominantly murine studies in this field may be extended to studying the dormancy paradigm directly in patients.

papers.title: Impaired IFN-γ/STAT1-associated immune regulation contributes to 4-nonylphenol-aggravated allergic rhinitis.
papers.authors: Li Z, Li J, Chen X, Liu Y.
papers.abstract: 4-Nonylphenol (4-NP) is a persistent endocrine-disrupting chemical, but its role in allergic rhinitis (AR) remains poorly understood. The study here integrated human transcriptomics, network toxicology, single-cell analysis, molecular modeling, and experimental validation to investigate the mechanisms underlying 4-NP-aggravated AR. Network analysis identified four shared candidates, e.g., CDKN1A , SKIL , IFNG , and B4GALT1 . In an independent cohort, IFNG and SKIL were down-regulated in AR, whereas CDKN1A was increased. Single-cell analysis showed that IFNG was mainly expressed in T-cells. Molecular docking predicted the strongest interaction between 4-NP and IFNγ (-6.4 kcal/mol), and a 50-ns molecular dynamics simulation supported the stability of the predicted complex. In human nasal epithelial progenitor cells (HNEPC), 4-NP increased IL1B , TNF , and IL6 expression. In house dust mite (HDM)-induced AR mice, 4-NP co-exposure increased nasal rubbing, eosinophilic inflammation, T H 2 responses, IL-4 production, and inflammatory gene expression, while reducing Ifng expression, T H 1 cells, and STAT1 phosphorylation. Recombinant IFNγ partially reversed the T H 1/T H 2 imbalance and reduced eosinophilic inflammation and IL-4 levels. These findings suggest that 4-NP aggravates AR in association with impaired IFNγ/STAT1-related immune regulation and enhanced nasal epithelial inflammation.

papers.title: Metabolic-Immune Crosstalk in Colorectal Cancer: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Opportunities.
papers.authors: Lu Y, Li X, Yuan X, Guo X, Chu D.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related morbidity and mortality worldwide, with its progression and therapeutic resistance increasingly recognized as consequences of complex metabolic and immune interactions within the tumour microenvironment (TME). Recent advances in single-cell and spatial multi-omics technologies have enabled detailed characterisation of metabolic heterogeneity among TME components, uncovering how distinct metabolic states influence immune function and therapeutic responses. In this review, we summarize recent advances in our understanding of metabolic regulation in the CRC microenvironment, with a particular focus on how distinct immune cell populations contribute to tumour progression and immune suppression through diverse metabolic pathways. We discuss key metabolite-driven signalling networks involving lactate, short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and amino acid derivatives, and examine how these pathways influence immune cell function and tumour-immune interactions. Furthermore, we highlight emerging therapeutic approaches targeting the metabolic-immune axis, including glutaminase inhibitors, CD36 antagonists, and combination regimens integrating metabolic intervention with immune checkpoint inhibitors. By integrating recent mechanistic discoveries with therapeutic perspectives, this review provides an updated overview of the metabolic-immune landscape in CRC and discusses potential strategies to exploit metabolic vulnerabilities for improving immunotherapy efficacy and overcoming treatment resistance.

papers.title: Single-cell profiling of the duodenum during chronic human norovirus infection.
papers.authors: Matsushima Y, Durkee-Shock J, Alves DA, Nagata BM, Kim SA, Chan EC, Chaimongkol N, Ishiyama R, Barton K, Han A, Kelly LA, Ogbogu PU, Kumar S, Xu X, Briggs KC, Murakami K, Cohen JI, Keller MD, Sosnovtsev SV, Green KY.
papers.abstract: Human noroviruses are a major cause of diarrheal disease, yet their pathogenesis remains poorly defined. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of duodenal biopsies and matched stem cell-derived enteroids from immunodeficient individuals with chronic norovirus infection. Norovirus RNA was detected primarily in enterocytes, enteroendocrine cells, and macrophages, with the highest proportion of viral RNA-positive cells observed among M2 macrophages, followed by late enterocytes. Despite this distribution, late enterocytes produced higher viral yields than differentiated M2 macrophages in vitro. Norovirus infection was associated with the up-regulation of MHC class I-related genes and IL15 in duodenal macrophages and late enterocytes, together with increased IFNG expression by CD8 T cells. Macrophages and late enterocytes up-regulated CXCL9 and CXCL10/11 , respectively, consistent with CD8 and CD4 T cell recruitment to the duodenum. These findings show that noroviruses infect and persist across multiple permissive cell types during chronic infection, resulting in marked dysregulation of innate and adaptive immune responses that may drive pathogenesis.

papers.title: Competing endogenous RNA networks in insects: Methodologies, physiological functions, and implications for pest management.
papers.authors: Han YJ, Khosravi Z, Lou YQ, Yang XL, Kashyap S, Liu YH, Liu SP.
papers.abstract: The competing endogenous RNA (ceRNA) hypothesis has reshaped our understanding of post-transcriptional regulation by revealing that coding and non-coding RNAs communicate through shared microRNA response elements. Insects, characterized by dramatic metamorphosis, complex life cycles, and strong environmental adaptability, are exceptional models for dissecting ceRNA networks. Recent advances in whole-transcriptome sequencing and bioinformatics have enabled systematic identification of ceRNA components-mRNAs, microRNAs, lncRNAs, and circRNAs-across insect taxa, facilitating network construction in development, reproduction, immunity, and insecticide resistance. This review synthesizes current methodologies, including component identification, target prediction, network assembly, and multi-level experimental validation through RT-qPCR, fluorescence in situ hybridization, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and RNA immunoprecipitation. We highlight key progress in circRNA/lncRNA-mediated regulation of intestinal development, chitin metabolism, molting, and senescence; sex-dimorphic modulation of fertility and oogenesis through nutrient-sensing axes; innate immune orchestration against fungal, bacterial, viral, and symbiotic challenges through Toll/Imd and redox pathways; and the dual contribution of cuticular barrier remodeling and detoxification enzyme activation to insecticide resistance. Despite these advances, major bottlenecks persist-a gap between omics-driven discovery and functional validation, ambiguous interaction specificity, scarcity of spatiotemporal and single-cell data, and fragmented links from molecular events to phenotypes. Future priorities include high-throughput functional screening, dynamic network modeling integrating temporal and spatial transcriptomics, stoichiometric quantification of competitive efficiency, multi-omics integration with transcriptional/epigenetic regulation, and RNAi-based strategies targeting core ceRNA nodes for green pest management. Elucidating the regulatory logic of insect ceRNA networks will reveal fundamental principles of post-transcriptional control and provide molecular targets for sustainable pest and vector control.

papers.title: Distinct cell-type-specific gene expression programs associated with persistence versus clearance of arterivirus infection.
papers.authors: Kapoor M, Chen C, Naru A, Hayes C, Herndon N, Bryne KA, Loving CL, Dekkers J, Tuggle CK, Fang Y.
papers.abstract: This study aims to identify cellular markers correlated to persistent viral infection by a comprehensive comparison of blood immune transcriptomes and cell composition from acute and long-term stages of infection using a porcine arterivirus as the model. We applied single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) to characterize blood mononuclear cells collected at 14 (acute) and 84 (long-term) days post-infection (DPI) with porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV). Pigs were grouped as persistently infected (PI, n = 5 at 14 DPI; n = 10 at 84 DPI) or virus-extinct (VE, n = 2) phenotypes based on detection of viral RNA in blood collected weekly and tissue samples collected at either 14 or 84 DPI. Monocytes emerged as the primary cellular drivers of infection outcome, with divergence driven mainly by cell-type-specific transcriptional programs rather than differences in immune cell compositions. At 14 DPI, genes expressed at higher levels in monocytes from VE pigs, which were enriched for activation of antiviral and interferon responses, and subsequently transitioned toward a homeostatic profile by 84 DPI. In contrast, monocytes from PI pigs were characterized by metabolic dysregulation at 14 DPI, followed by a chronic inflammation profile at 84 DPI. Temporal analysis revealed the "when and how" rather than the intensity of immune activation as a critical determinant of outcome, with PI pigs failing to mount early, effective antiviral responses. Collectively, these findings identified early monocyte transcriptional programs associated with PRRSV persistence, offering a potential application in the selection of biomarkers for disease surveillance and outbreak management in swine production.IMPORTANCEPersistent viral infection remains a critical challenge in human health, as well as livestock disease management, yet the viral-host immune mechanisms that determine whether infection resolves or persists remain poorly understood. This study used a swine arterivirus persistent infection model system along with advanced single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) technology to address a broad biological significance question-how circulating immune cell-type-specific transcriptional programs at early stages of infection determine long-term viral outcomes in the host. This work generated the first scRNA-seq data set for porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus (PRRSV) persistent infection and provides a framework for mining cell-type-resolved blood transcriptomes, which could assist in developing therapeutic strategies to manipulate host immune responses toward viral extinction pathways during infection.

papers.title: Establishment and validation of a diagnostic model for Kawasaki disease based on cell adhesion molecule-related genes and analysis of immune-related features.
papers.authors: Shao Z, Ruan Z, Sheng F, Su C.
papers.abstract: Background In children, Kawasaki disease (KD) - characterized by immune dysregulation and vasculitis - represents the most common cause of acquired heart disease. Although cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) contribute significantly to the vascular inflammation observed in KD, how they act synergistically and how this knowledge might be applied clinically remain poorly understood. Methods Leveraging multiple public KD transcriptomic datasets, we identified differentially expressed CAM-related genes through differential expression analysis and WGCNA, then used four machine learning algorithms (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator, eXtreme Gradient Boosting, random forest, and support vector machine recursive feature elimination) to build a six-gene diagnostic model. Immune infiltration was assessed via single sample Gene Set Enrichment Analysis, CIBERSORT, and MCP-Counter, and molecular subtyping with functional enrichment by clusterProfiler. Results This study pinpointed six core diagnostic genes. The model built from them showed excellent discriminative ability across training and several independent validation datasets. Immune profiling revealed a KD microenvironment skewed by overabundant innate immune cells (neutrophils, monocytes, macrophages) and marked deficiency of adaptive immune cells (CD8+ T cells, NK cells, B cells). Using these genes, patients split into two molecular subtypes, with subtype 2 featuring enhanced adaptive immune infiltration. Conclusion A six-gene KD diagnostic model is proposed here, revealing immune imbalance, molecular subtypes, and potential drug targets, and offering novel insights into CAM-associated pathways.

papers.title: Predictive value of systemic inflammatory indices for new-onset atrial fibrillation after acute myocardial infarction: an interpretable machine learning study.
papers.authors: Meng X, Wen Y, Zhan G, Xia Y, Wang X, Ma C, Xia Y, Yang X, Gao L.
papers.abstract: Background New-onset atrial fibrillation (NOAF) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is associated with adverse outcomes. Inflammation contributes to atrial fibrillation (AF) onset and progression. We developed an interpretable machine learning (ML) framework integrating complete blood count (CBC)-derived inflammatory indices with routine clinical parameters for NOAF risk assessment. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 3,077 AMI patients without prior AF (2018-2023). Multivariable logistic regression, restricted cubic splines (RCS), and threshold analyses evaluated six inflammatory indices: neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), systemic immune-inflammation index (SII), monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR), systemic inflammation response index (SIRI), and aggregate index of systemic inflammation (AISI). Boruta and LASSO selections were intersected. Eight ML models were evaluated, with Shapley Additive Explanations (SHAP) for interpretation. Results NOAF incidence was 7.73%. Six indices were associated with NOAF in separate adjusted models (all p Conclusions CBC-derived inflammatory indices were associated with NOAF, but their incremental predictive value beyond routine clinical variables remains uncertain. Given moderate predictive performance and no external validation, multicenter validation is needed before clinical implementation.

papers.title: Discovery of novel small-molecule binders targeting IL-6 receptor conformational ensembles to regulate IL-6 signaling.
papers.authors: Yang J, Fu B, Du Q, Lin X, He Y, Wu H, Xue W.
papers.abstract: Introduction Interleukin-6 (IL-6) signaling via its receptor (IL-6R) is a central driver of inflammation and immune-related diseases. Although monoclonal antibodies targeting this pathway are clinically effective, their limitations, including high costs and parenteral administration, create an urgent need for orally available small-molecule inhibitors. However, targeting the extensive protein‒protein interaction interface between IL-6 and IL-6R remains a significant challenge. Objectives This study aims to discover novel small-molecule inhibitors that directly bind to IL-6R and disrupt IL-6/IL-6R complex formation through an integrated computational and experimental strategy while also delineating the druggable binding site on IL-6R to guide rational drug design. Methods Ensemble docking was performed against thirteen distinct IL-6R conformations to screen five diverse compound libraries totaling 98,992 molecules. Iterative rounds of molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, accumulating 78.35 μs, were employed to refine candidate selection. In vitro evaluations included STAT3 luciferase reporter assays, western blotting, flow cytometry, cell proliferation assays, cytotoxicity assays, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), and biolayer interferometry (BLI). Site-directed mutagenesis and long-timescale MD simulations validated the binding site. Results Nineteen compounds were experimentally evaluated, identifying Z1268663363 and Z1268663684 as potent IL-6 signaling inhibitors. Both compounds suppressed IL-6-induced STAT3, JAK1, JAK2, ERK1/2, and gp130 phosphorylation and inhibited IL-6-dependent TF-1 cell proliferation. SPR and BLI confirmed direct binding to IL-6R (Kd = 14.83 μM and 8.27 μM) and disruption of IL-6/IL-6R complex formation. Mutagenesis validated residues Y249 and E296 as critical for binding. Two additional analogs, Z1268663546 and Z1268663944, also exhibited inhibitory activity against IL-6 signaling. Conclusion This study delineates a druggable small-molecule binding site on IL-6R and identifies four novel inhibitors with validated on-target activity, providing a critical foundation for developing next-generation oral therapies for IL-6-driven diseases.

papers.title: 3D Bioprinting as an In Vitro Tool to Model the Tumor Microenvironment.
papers.authors: Mantaka Z, Shteinberg E, Le Roux M, Mirani B, Willerth SM.
papers.abstract: Three‑dimensional (3D) bioprinting has rapidly emerged as a powerful strategy for engineering physiologically relevant tumor microenvironment (TME) models that overcome the limitations of traditional 2D cultures and animal systems. The TME is a highly dynamic and heterogeneous ecosystem composed of malignant, stromal, immune, and vascular cells embedded within a biochemically and mechanically complex extracellular matrix (ECM). These components collectively regulate tumor progression, immune evasion, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Conventional preclinical models fail to capture this complexity, contributing to poor clinical translation of oncology therapeutics. Advances in extrusion‑based, inkjet, laser‑assisted, and stereolithographic bioprinting now enable spatially organized, multicellular constructs with tunable biochemical and biophysical cues that more accurately recapitulate TME architecture and function. Complementary innovations in biomaterials, microfluidics, and computational modeling further expand the capabilities of bioprinted systems for drug screening, mechanistic studies, and personalized medicine. This review summarizes the cellular and acellular components of the TME, outlines major bioprinting technologies and biomaterial strategies, and highlights emerging applications in cancer modeling. We also identify key research gaps and opportunities that must be addressed to advance bioprinted TME platforms toward robust, standardized, and clinically meaningful tools for precision oncology.

papers.title: Normalized membrane ratio of TROP2 as a predictor of clinical outcomes with datopotamab deruxtecan in non-small-cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Garassino MC, Ahn MJ, Schick M, Kapil A, Paz-Ares L, Lisberg A, Johnson ML, Pérol M, Shimizu T, Heist R, Spira A, Okamoto I, Girard N, Cornelissen R, Pons-Tostivint E, Hong MH, Zwirtes R, Chiaverelli R, Rebelatto M, Sung M, Deng C, Harper J, Carroll D, Sade H, Sands J.
papers.abstract: Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd)-a trophoblast cell surface antigen 2 (TROP2)-directed antibody-drug conjugate-has demonstrated efficacy in patients with advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) ± actionable genomic alterations. However, TROP2 expression by pathologist assessment using conventional immunohistochemistry with visual scoring does not predict response to TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugates in NSCLC. We developed TROP2 quantitative continuous scoring (QCS)-a fully supervised computational pathology approach that quantifies TROP2 expression in individual NSCLC cells and subcellular components from immunohistochemistry-stained slides. Using QCS to determine TROP2 expression at the tumor cell membrane and cytoplasm, normalized membrane ratio (NMR) was developed (ratio of membrane relative to membrane + cytoplasmic TROP2) in the biomarker-evaluable population of patients with advanced NSCLC in the TROPION-PanTumor01 study (n = 115). The TROP2 NMR cut-point was optimized and validated in patients with nonsquamous NSCLC without actionable genomic alterations (primary intended-use population, n = 221) in the biomarker-evaluable population (n = 352) of the TROPION-Lung01 trial. Association with clinical outcomes was assessed. Progression-free survival was longer in Dato-DXd-treated (median 7.2 versus 4.0 months; hazard ratio 0.40, 95% confidence interval 0.25-0.64) but not docetaxel-treated (median 4.1 versus 4.4 months; hazard ratio 0.94, 95% confidence interval 0.59-1.49) patients with TROP2 NMR-positive versus TROP2 NMR-negative samples (treatment by biomarker status interaction P = 0.0098), indicating that TROP2 NMR may be a predictive biomarker for Dato-DXd.

papers.title: Cell Reprogramming: Therapeutic Advances and Challenges.
papers.authors: Li A, Wang Z, Lyu Z, Tuo Z, Li X, Wu RC, Wang J, Wusiman D, Wang Y, Zhang Q, Xiong W, Zhou B, Feng D.
papers.abstract: Cell reprogramming, which forcibly alters cell fate, offers a novel therapeutic strategy for various refractory diseases. Unlike previous reviews focused on a single disease context or a single reprogramming modality, this review is organized around therapeutic applications. It summarizes advances in direct reprogramming, partial reprogramming, and cell fusion-induced reprogramming and further compares their mechanisms, challenges in clinical translation, and safety boundaries. In oncology, reprogramming cancer cells into antigen-presenting cells elicits durable antitumor immunity and remodels the tumor microenvironment, whereas converting cancer cells into nonmalignant somatic cells can reduce their malignant phenotype and tumorigenic potential. In neurodegenerative diseases, direct reprogramming has converted fibroblasts or astrocytes into functional dopaminergic and cortical neurons both in vitro and in vivo. In mouse models of progeria and natural aging, partial reprogramming strategies markedly extend lifespan, ameliorate multiorgan pathology, and enhance tissue regenerative capacity. However, the strength and reproducibility of these findings vary across experimental models, and reported therapeutic benefits do not necessarily establish complete, stable, or safe cell-fate conversion. Against this predominantly preclinical background, ER-100 is the first regenerative therapy based on partial epigenetic reprogramming to receive Food and Drug Administration Investigational New Drug approval and enter clinical testing. It therefore provides an important reference point for the transition from animal studies to human trials. Cell fusion-induced reprogramming has context-dependent roles in tumor immunity. Fusion between tumor cells and immune cells may promote malignant progression. In contrast, dendritic cell-tumor cell fusion vaccines and chimeric exosomes can activate antitumor immune responses in preclinical models and early clinical studies. Major barriers to clinical translation include low reprogramming efficiency, an incompletely defined safety window, and the need to select in vivo or ex vivo strategies according to disease context. In addition, insufficient delivery efficiency, poor targeting, and long-term tumorigenic risk remain important constraints on clinical application. Looking ahead, single-cell multiomics and artificial intelligence may help optimize reprogramming factor combinations, while nonviral systems may improve targeted delivery. Integration with tissue engineering may further facilitate clinical translation across oncology, aging, regenerative medicine, autoimmune diseases, and neuropsychiatric disorders.

Transcription factors, small molecules, or the intratumoral vaccination chimera (iVAC) can convert cancer cells into conventional type 1 dendritic cells (cDC1s) or antigen-presenting cell (APC)-like cells. These reprogrammed cells enhance antigen presentation, activate CD8 + T-cell responses, and remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment into an immune-activated state. The resulting expansion of effector and memory T-cell populations may support tumor regression and durable antitumor immune protection; (B) Reprogramming cancer cells into nonmalignant somatic-like cells. Transcription factors or small molecules can redirect cancer cells toward hepatocyte-, melanocyte-, or adipocyte-like states, thereby suppressing proliferation, invasion, metastasis, and tumorigenic potential. However, phenotypic conversion does not necessarily eliminate the original oncogenic alterations, and long-term stability and safety require further evaluation. papers.title: Multi-omics integration reveals a gut microbiota-metabolite-immune axis in PFOA-induced intestinal toxicity.
papers.authors: Wang KW, Liu W, Yeerbolati Y, Ding Z, Xu C, Yu L, Yan X, Cheng JQ, Deng C, Huang J.
papers.abstract: Perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) is a persistent environmental contaminant associated with immunometabolic toxicity; however, its effects on the intestinal microenvironment remain incompletely understood. We integrated a murine PFOA exposure model with untargeted serum metabolomics, 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and single-cell RNA sequencing to characterize intestinal injury and explore microbiota-metabolite-immune relationships. PFOA exposure caused dose-dependent body weight loss, colon shortening, histopathological injury, disrupted epithelial junctional staining, and increased proinflammatory cytokine concentrations. It was also associated with restructuring of the gut microbiota and broad alterations in serum tryptophan-related metabolites, including a metabolomic feature putatively annotated as indole-3-propionic acid (IPA), whose normalized relative abundance was reduced. Single-cell analyses indicated remodeling of epithelial, T-cell, and fibroblast states, including enrichment of a T helper 1 (Th1)-like transcriptional program and altered fibroblast-associated inflammatory pathways. IPA supplementation partially ameliorated several PFOA-associated intestinal and inflammatory phenotypes but did not broadly normalize α-diversity, β-diversity, the relative abundance of Clostridium, or the fibroblast-associated markers examined. In polarized murine Th1 cells, IPA reduced JAK2 and STAT3 phosphorylation; this effect was partially attenuated by the AhR antagonist CH-223191, consistent with AhR-dependent restraint of JAK-STAT signaling. CellChat analysis further identified computationally inferred changes in selected CD44-associated ligand-receptor pairs between fibroblasts and Th1 cells. Collectively, these findings support a model in which PFOA-associated perturbation of microbial tryptophan metabolism and IPA-related signaling may contribute to epithelial and immune dysfunction.

papers.title: Multi-Omics Mendelian Randomization Identifies DDX17 as a Potential Mediator Linking Gut Microbiota-Immune-Metabolism Axis to Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.authors: Xiao Z, Qin Y, Dong M, Wei S, Ma Q, Luo C, Li Y, Chen F, Wu G, Wei P, Hu R, Huang Z, Liu C.
papers.abstract: Introduction The gut microbiota-immune-metabolism axis has been implicated in Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathogenesis; however, the key host molecular targets linking peripheral dysregulation to central neurodegeneration remain elusive. Methods In this study, we systematically integrated large-scale GWAS data covering 1,903 gut microbiota taxa, 14,696 immune cell features, and 34,843 metabolite features with AD GWAS summary statistics, using two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to identify causal genes. These genes were intersected with differentially expressed genes from three GEO datasets, followed by protein-protein interaction network construction using four Cytoscape algorithms (MCC, EPC, DMNC, Degree) and feature selection via three machine learning methods (Support Vector Machine, Random Forest, LASSO). Single-cell transcriptomics (GSE188545) localized key gene expression, Support Vector Machine virtual knockout (scTenifoldKnk) analyzed downstream regulatory networks, with in vitro validation performed in okadaic acid-treated SH-SY5Y cells using RT-qPCR and Western blotting. Results MR analysis revealed multiple causal associations among microbial taxa, immune phenotypes, metabolites, and AD. Integration of MR causal genes with DEGs, PPI network analysis, and machine learning refinement prioritized six key genes: BYSL, DDX17, HSPA6, RRN3, C4B, and NCKAP1L. Among them, only DDX17 showed robust expression in AD-associated neuronal populations in single-cell transcriptomics, whereas the other five genes showed low expression and may act through non-cell-autonomous mechanisms. Virtual knockout predicted that the PI3K/AKT pathway was the most significantly enriched downstream of DDX17 perturbation. In vitro, DDX17 was significantly upregulated in an OA-induced AD cell model, and siRNA-mediated knockdown partially reversed tau hyperphosphorylation (total P-tau and P-tau Thr217), while restoring AKT phosphorylation at Thr308 and Ser473. Conclusion These findings suggest that DDX17 is a potential downstream host candidate linking peripheral dysregulation to tau pathology in AD, partially through PI3K/AKT pathway modulation. However, these results are primarily hypothesis-generating, and direct mechanistic and in vivo validation remain essential.

papers.title: A computational tool to predict how new coronavirus variants evade antibody defenses.
papers.authors: Kalmotia V, Roy S, Amsaad F.
papers.abstract: The emergence of SARS-CoV-2 variants with mutations in the receptor-binding domain (RBD) poses a significant challenge to antibody-mediated immunity and ongoing vaccine effectiveness. In this work, we present RBD-Escape, a transparent and experimentally grounded computational framework for estimating how combinations of RBD mutations influence recognition by polyclonal neutralizing antibodies. The framework integrates deep mutational scanning (DMS) measurements from 33 monoclonal antibodies characterized across multiple independent studies and aggregates these data into a unified model of antibody escape. Unlike black-box predictive approaches, RBD-Escape directly leverages experimentally measured escape profiles, providing an interpretable representation of mutation-driven immune evasion. The proposed framework estimates the impact of arbitrary mutation combinations by modeling both additive and redundant antibody escape effects. Validation against independent neutralization datasets demonstrates strong agreement between predicted binding scores and experimentally measured neutralization outcomes, indicating that aggregated DMS data can effectively capture major patterns of antibody escape. Application of the framework to the Omicron variant revealed extensive predicted reductions in antibody recognition relative to earlier SARS-CoV-2 variants, consistent with its observed immune-evasive properties. In addition to quantitative escape prediction, RBD-Escape provides interactive visualization capabilities that facilitate exploration of mutation-specific and variant-level escape patterns. Although the current implementation focuses exclusively on mutations within the RBD and does not account for contributions from other spike protein regions, it offers a rapid, interpretable, and experiment-driven approach for evaluating emerging variants. The framework has potential applications in genomic surveillance, vaccine evaluation, and the assessment of mutation-driven antigenic change, but predictions should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than definitive (Lucas et al., 2021).

papers.title: The Role of Tumor-Associated Macrophages in Lung Cancer Progression and Therapy: From Mechanistic Insights to Targeting Strategies.
papers.authors: Sun J, Liu Y, Sun H, Shen Y, Xue F.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are among the most abundant immune cells in the lung cancer tumor microenvironment (TME), where their functions vary according to developmental origin, local signals, metabolic conditions, spatial location, and treatment exposure. The conventional M1 and M2 framework therefore does not adequately represent the diversity of macrophage states in human tumors. This narrative review examines the origin of TAMs in lung cancer, their context-dependent functional states, spatial organization, and interactions with current treatments in non-small cell lung cancer and small cell lung cancer. Single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics have identified macrophage populations associated with primary tumors and specific metastatic sites. Mechanistic studies further implicate cytokine signalling, extracellular vesicle communication, metabolic regulation, and phagocytosis checkpoints in tumor cell proliferation, stemness maintenance, epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), angiogenesis and the formation of an immunosuppressive microenvironment. TAMs can contribute to tumor clearance in some settings but promote immune suppression, tissue repair, and treatment resistance in others. Targeting strategies directed against TAMs, including inhibition of monocyte recruitment, modification of tumor-supportive macrophage states, blockade of phagocytosis checkpoints, and macrophage-directed drug delivery, have demonstrated activity primarily in experimental lung cancer models. However, clinical studies have not yet established the efficacy, selectivity, or safety of these approaches. Major challenges remain, including the high heterogeneity of TAMs, activation of compensatory pathways, systemic toxicity, and the translational gap between preclinical and clinical studies. Future research should focus on validating markers that distinguish disease-associated macrophage states from macrophages required for pulmonary homeostasis and integrating longitudinal tissue, circulating, spatial, and imaging biomarkers. Controlled clinical studies are required to determine whether macrophage-directed interventions can improve existing lung cancer treatments.

figure.caption: Origins, regulatory cues, and functional plasticity of TAMs in lung cancer. ( A ) TAMs include self-renewing alveolar macrophages derived mainly from fetal monocytes and macrophages generated from recruited circulating monocytes. CCL2/CCR2 and CX3CL1/CX3CR1 regulate monocyte recruitment, whereas CSF1/CSF1R supports macrophage differentiation and survival. ( B ) Cytokines, extracellular vesicles, and metabolic factors shape context-dependent inflammatory and immunoregulatory macrophage programs through pathways including JAK/STAT and PI3K/AKT. Bidirectional arrows indicate macrophage plasticity rather than fixed cellular identities. ( C ) These states may support phagocytosis and T-cell recruitment or promote tumor-cell proliferation, angiogenesis, EMT, immunosuppression, metastasis, and immune evasion. Solid arrows indicate recruitment, induction, or functional effects, and the circular arrow indicates local self-renewal. Green elements indicate tumor-restrictive functions, whereas red bars indicate tumor-supportive outcomes. Bold text highlights key cell populations, macrophage states, and functional processes. Evidence is mainly preclinical or associative. papers.title: Harnessing the Immune System in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Targeting: Mechanistic Insights and Therapeutic Potential of Natural Products and Traditional Chinese Medicine.
papers.authors: Hao L, Li L, Chen Y, Gao J, Xie Y, Li Q, Lu J, Zhang Z.
papers.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is highly malignant, and most patients are diagnosed at intermediate or advanced stages. Current regimens, including surgery, targeted therapy and immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), are limited by low response rates, drug resistance, prominent toxicities and high costs, so safe and effective combination strategies are urgently needed. Natural products and traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exert multi-target, multi-pathway and bidirectional immunomodulatory effects, remodel the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) of liver cancer, and synergize with immunotherapy, with promising clinical significance as adjuncts to standard treatments. This review systematically summarizes the cellular and non-cellular components of the HCC immune microenvironment and the molecular mechanisms by which natural medicines reverse tumor immune escape and improve immunotherapy sensitivity, covering regulation of immune cells, interference with PD-1/PD-L1, CTLA-4 and TIM-3 pathways, targeting of cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) and the extracellular matrix, modulation of chemokine networks, and inhibition of tumor angiogenesis. Preclinical evidence supporting efficacy enhancement and toxicity reduction upon combination of natural medicines with targeted agents, ICIs, radiotherapy and chemotherapy is also summarized. Current challenges, including tumor heterogeneity, low bioavailability, lack of unified quality standards and insufficient translational evidence, are analyzed, and future directions such as single-cell and spatial multi-omics, nano-delivery systems and gut microbiome analysis are proposed to accelerate mechanism-driven personalized combinations and standardized clinical trials, providing a theoretical basis for the clinical application of natural products and TCM in liver cancer immunotherapy.

figure.label: Figure 1
figure.caption: Overall components of the tumor immune microenvironment in HCC. Tumor cells, various immune cells (including exhausted CD8 + T cells, Tregs, M2-type TAMs, NK cells, etc), cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs), extracellular matrix (ECM), cytokines/chemokines and pro-angiogenic mediators interact with each other to form an immunosuppressive niche, which drives tumor progression and resistance to immunotherapy.

papers.title: White Blood Cell Count-related Biomarkers for Acute Myocardial Infarction: Integrative Analysis of Mouse Models and Clinical Samples.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Yang M.
papers.abstract: Introduction Although white blood cell count (WBC) is an accessible prognostic marker, the relationship between WBC-related genes and outcomes in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains unclear. Methods A retrospective study of 1,917 patients with AMI was conducted to estimate prognostic indicators. Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was used to identify potential genes associated with the prognostic indicators, and the resulting genes were intersected with differentially expressed genes from the key monocyte subset identified in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analyses. Key genes were screened by integrating 52 machine learning algorithms. The expression of key genes was validated by RT-qPCR with clinical samples. In addition, an AMI mouse model was established, and the expression of related proteins was further validated by western blotting and immunohistochemistry. Results Age, WBC, and serum potassium (K) level were identified as prognostic indicators for AMI. Eight key genes were identified. Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) showed that these genes were significantly enriched in immune- and inflammation-related pathways. RT-qPCR validation showed that the expression trends of five key genes (ITGA4, RASA3, ATG7, HSPA6, and ITGAM) were consistent with the bioinformatics results, whereas DSTN, FES, and MCL1 did not reach statistical significance. Additionally, WB and IHC further validated HSP70 family protein upregulation in the AMI mouse model. Discussion Eight AMI-related genes were identified and might contribute to disease progression through inflammatory regulation. The integration of multi-omics analysis and experimental validation underscores the translational potential of these genes. Although further experimental validation is warranted, these findings may offer novel insights for the development of therapeutic strategies for AMI. Conclusion This study identified eight key WBC-related genes that may serve as potential biomarkers for AMI.
