papers.title: CHMP5 Is a TCR- and Interleukin-7-Regulated Protein Required for Naïve T Cell Homeostasis.
papers.authors: Trichka J, Umphred-Wilson K, Bak E, Liao YC, Shim JH, Adoro S.
papers.abstract: A diverse repertoire of naïve αβ T cells in the periphery is essential for adaptive immunity to pathogens and cancers, as well as for tissue homeostasis. This peripheral T cell pool is maintained by signals from the T cell receptor (TCR) and interleukin-7 (IL-7). However, the mechanisms and downstream factors induced by these signals to support peripheral T cell survival are still not fully understood. We found that TCR and IL-7 signals posttranscriptionally promoted expression of the charged multivesicular body protein 5 (CHMP5) in naïve CD4 + and CD8 + T cells, in which CHMP5 functions to prevent oxidative stress and apoptosis. Consequently, inactivation of the Chmp5 gene in post-thymic T cells resulted in severe depletion of the peripheral T cell pool by a cell-intrinsic mechanism. Collectively, our results suggest that induction of CHMP5 by homeostatic TCR and IL-7 signals is part of a critical mechanism governing naïve T cell homeostasis in the periphery.

papers.title: CRAFT: an antigen-specific TCR generative model for conditional de novo design with physicochemical constraints.
papers.authors: Yang X, Li Z, Li Z, Zhang W, Zhang X, Yang T, Liu M, Li X.
papers.abstract: T-cell receptors (TCRs) are essential to adaptive immunity and mediate the recognition and elimination of malignant or infected cells through antigen-specific interactions. Despite the clinical progress of TCR-based immunotherapies, computational de novo design of antigen-specific TCRs remains difficult. The main difficulties include the complexity of peptide-major histocompatibility complex (pMHC)-dependent recognition, strict physicochemical requirements at the binding interface, and the small amount of paired training data available for model development. Current generative approaches depend largely on 1D sequence statistics and do not capture pMHC presentation context, interfacial physicochemical properties, and native receptor priors within a unified framework. We present conditional reconstruction of antigen fragments for TCRs (CRAFT), a decoupled generative model for pMHC-conditioned de novo design of antigen-specific TCR CDR3$\beta $ sequences under physicochemical constraints. With large-scale pretraining, CRAFT learns base representations that help reduce the limitations imposed by data scarcity. We further incorporate antigen-derived contextual information to guide antigen-specific TCR CDR3$\beta $ sequence design. The architecture comprises an antigen encoder (PrimeBERT) that captures the pMHC context and an autoregressive decoder (PrimeTCR) that preserves native receptor priors. The encoder and decoder are coupled through cross-attention and augmented with Atchley factor embeddings, allowing CRAFT to incorporate physicochemical constraints relevant to antigen-conditioned receptor design during sequence decoding. Across multiple evaluations, CRAFT demonstrates competitive sequence naturalness, together with favorable performance in specific binding, and predicted structural plausibility. Overall, CRAFT provides a computational framework for developing personalized tumor immunotherapies. It also holds potential to support clinical translation by enabling the efficient, targeted discovery of candidate TCRs.

papers.title: Screening Strategies Among High-Risk Populations for Anal Cancer (ACCESS Study) Protocol.
papers.authors: Subbiah R, Bangera SR, Kaonga NN, Tadros MG, Rosa-Cuhna I, Jeudin PP, Lymon KJ, Ciers-Davis NA, Reyes A, Govindaraj S, Garcia-Buitrago MT, Mehta CC, Galli JH, Potter JE, Peters M, Smith AK, Ibegbu C, Mosanjac M, Velu V, Xiao C, Flowers L.
papers.abstract: Background Anal cancer is a human papillomavirus (HPV)-associated malignancy that disproportionately affects high-risk populations, including people living with HIV, men who have sex with men, and women with a history of high-grade lower genital tract neoplasia. Persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV) is the primary cause of anal high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions (aHSIL), the precursor to anal cancer. Current screening approaches, including anal cytology and high-resolution anoscopy (HRA), have important limitations related to diagnostic performance, cost, accessibility, and the availability of trained providers. There is a critical need for improved screening strategies and biomarkers capable of identifying individuals at greatest risk of persistent disease and progression. Methods The screening strategies among high-risk populations for anal cancer (ACCESS) study is a prospective, multisite, longitudinal cohort study that will enroll 500 high-risk adults from Emory University and the University of Miami. Participants will undergo annual screening for up to 2 years using anal cytology, hrHPV genotyping, CINtec®PLUS dual staining, HRA, and biopsy when indicated. Anal swabs, biopsies, and optional peripheral blood samples will be collected for molecular and immunologic analyses. DNA methylation markers, inflammatory biomarkers, immune profiling by multicolor flow cytometry, and single-cell RNA sequencing will be evaluated to assess their association with aHSIL prevalence and clearance. Diagnostic performance measures, multivariable regression analyses, and biomarker-based predictive models will be used to evaluate study outcomes. Discussion The ACCESS study will evaluate the performance of emerging screening biomarkers and characterize molecular and immune pathways associated with anal carcinogenesis in diverse high-risk populations. By integrating clinical, epigenetic, immunologic, and environmental data, this study aims to improve risk stratification, identify biomarkers associated with persistent disease, and inform the development of more effective and targeted anal cancer prevention strategies. © 2026 The Author(s). papers.title: Screening of oxidative stress-related signature genes and construction of an interpretable discriminant model for preeclampsia.
papers.authors: Tian L, Ma X, Zhang Y, Hao T, Wang H, Meng H, Xin H.
papers.abstract: Background Preeclampsia (PE) is a serious pregnancy complication threatening maternal and fetal health, and its onset and progression are closely associated with placental oxidative stress. However, a systematic understanding of oxidative stress-related genes in PE and their roles in immune regulation remains lacking. Objective To identify oxidative stress-related signature genes in preeclampsia, validate their expression and tissue localization in placental tissues, construct an interpretable machine learning discriminant model, and explore their relationship with placental immune infiltration. Methods Nine GEO datasets were classified into three groups: a feature gene screening group (GSE10588, GSE75010), an artificial neural network training group (GSE30186, GSE44711, GSE54618, GSE24129, GSE43942, GSE147776), and an independent validation group (GSE25906). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified by limma, and their intersection with oxidative stress-related genes yielded candidate DEOSRGs. Multi-algorithm recursive feature elimination (SVM-RFE, RF-RFE, XGB-RFE) with five-fold cross-validation selected the core signature genes. Placental protein expression and trophoblast localization were assessed in clinical specimens (50 PE vs. 50 controls). An artificial neural network (ANN) discriminant model was constructed on the training group, with GSE25906 used for independent validation and SHAP-based interpretability analysis. Immune infiltration was analyzed by CIBERSORT on GSE75010. Results We identified 87 DEGs (65 upregulated, 22 downregulated) and 17 candidate DEOSRGs. Consensus recursive feature elimination screening yielded five core signature genes: LEP, HK2, NDRG1, membrane metallo-endopeptidase, and SERPINA3. Western blotting confirmed significant upregulation of all five proteins in PE placental tissues (P Conclusion Five oxidative stress-related signature genes (LEP, HK2, NDRG1, MME, and SERPINA3) were identified and found significantly upregulated in PE placental tissues. An interpretable neural network discriminant model was constructed and independently validated. These biomarkers reflect placental pathophysiological alterations and may contribute to PE progression through coordinated modulation of oxidative stress and the maternal-fetal immune microenvironment.

papers.title: SingleRepExplorer: a unified interactive platform for integrated single-cell transcriptomic and immune repertoire analysis.
papers.authors: Ishikawa M.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing coupled with V(D)J repertoire profiling enables simultaneous capture of lymphocyte transcriptomes and paired antigen receptor sequences, yet analysis of these multimodal datasets remains a substantial barrier for experimental immunologists. Existing graphical platforms either focus exclusively on transcriptomics or treat repertoire data as a secondary annotation, lacking the deep integration required for systems immunology. Here, I present SingleRepExplorer, a comprehensive, code-free analytical platform designed for 10x Genomics Cell Ranger output, built with R/Shiny, and distributed as a Docker container. The platform unifies transcriptomic preprocessing with Seurat, immune repertoire profiling with scRepertoire and immunarch, receptor-transcriptome multimodal correlation with CoNGA, cell-cell communication inference with CellChat, B-cell phylogenetic lineage reconstruction, CDR3 sequence-similarity networking, and CDR3 physicochemical characterization within a single interactive interface. Interface features include a Memory-Preserved Quality Control module for iterative threshold adjustment without data reload, JavaScript-based Lasso cell selection for interactive subclustering, and direct export of publication-ready editable vector graphics. I applied SingleRepExplorer to a publicly available pooled PBMC dataset from COVID-19 healthcare workers and vaccinated individuals. Without writing code, I observed a massively expanded cytotoxic T lymphocyte clonotype in the HCW_convalescent condition, characterized its diversity metrics, linked it to a transcriptionally distinct effector cluster expressing GNLY, GZMH, NKG7, and CD8A, and mapped its exploratory intercellular signaling footprint, highlighting Cluster 7-derived MIF and CCL5-CCR4 axes within the HCW_convalescent network. These illustrative results demonstrate that SingleRepExplorer enables an experimental immunologist to carry a dataset from raw sequencing output to systems-level hypotheses entirely through a graphical interface, and benchmarking of the platform's core modules against independent reference workflows is reported alongside. The platform is freely available at https://github.com/amufaamo/SingleRepExplorer.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics links amino acid metabolism-related biomarkers to endothelial immune remodeling in periodontitis.
papers.authors: Wu H, Liu X, Zhu Y, Guo M, Wang M, Chen M, Liu X.
papers.abstract: Background Periodontitis (PD) is a chronic inflammatory disease driven by microbial dysbiosis and immune-mediated periodontal tissue destruction. Although amino acid metabolic dysregulation has been implicated in inflammatory diseases, its diagnostic relevance and cellular context in PD remain unclear. We aimed to identify amino acid metabolism-related diagnostic biomarkers and characterize their potential roles in PD. Methods Bulk transcriptomic datasets (GSE16134, GSE10334, and GSE223924) and a single-cell RNA sequencing dataset (GSE164241) were analyzed. Amino acid metabolism-related differentially expressed genes were identified and functionally annotated through enrichment analyses. LASSO regression, Boruta, and random forest jointly screened diagnostic biomarkers. A nomogram was constructed and assessed by ROC, calibration, and decision curve analyses. Immune infiltration, consensus clustering, and weighted gene co-expression network analysis were performed; cell-type localization, cell-cell communication, and pseudotime analyses used single-cell data. Human gingival tissue samples were used for validation through histological analysis, immunohistochemistry, and quantitative real-time PCR (RT-qPCR). Results Six amino acid metabolism-related biomarkers showed concordant expression changes across the three bulk datasets. TDO2, ICAM2, VWF and FABP4 were upregulated in periodontitis, whereas ACAT2 and AHNAK2 were downregulated. The six-gene nomogram discriminated PD from controls in GSE16134 (AUC = 0.956), while cross-platform evaluation revealed calibration limitations. Enrichment analysis linked these biomarkers to chemokine and cytokine signaling, cell adhesion and leukocyte transendothelial migration. Immune infiltration and consensus clustering revealed broad immune associations and three expression-based subgroups with distinct inflammatory features. Single-cell analysis localized the highest biomarker activity to endothelial cells, which showed the strongest diagnostic biomarker module score despite a relative reduction in their proportion. Pseudotime analysis revealed biomarker expression variation along an inferred endothelial trajectory, while CellChat predicted altered endothelial-immune communication. Experimental validation confirmed these changes for TDO2, ICAM2, VWF, FABP4 and ACAT2 at both mRNA and protein levels in clinical samples. Conclusion We identify six amino acid metabolism-related candidate biomarkers with diagnostic potential for PD-five supported by clinical gingival tissue expression data-and link them to endothelial cell state changes and immune microenvironment remodeling. These findings provide an immune-metabolic framework for biomarker development and mechanistic studies in PD.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics and machine learning identify mechanical stimulus-related genes and immune microenvironment remodeling in heart failure.
papers.authors: Zhang C, Zhao L, Sun J, Wang X, Zhang C, Li A.
papers.abstract: Background Heart failure (HF) is a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, driven by complex pathophysiological processes including abnormal mechanical stress and immune microenvironment remodeling. Although mechanical stimulus is known to trigger maladaptive cardiac remodeling, the systematic role of mechanical stimulus-related genes (MSRGs) in HF diagnosis and immune modulation remains poorly defined. This study aims to identify MSRG-based diagnostic biomarkers, characterize molecular subtypes, and explore their cellular localization and immune microenvironment interactions in HF. Methods Bulk transcriptomic data and MSigDB-curated MSRGs were analyzed. Differential expression screening identified MSRGs altered between HF and healthy specimens. Three algorithms-Random Forest, LASSO, and SVM-RFE-were jointly applied to select diagnostic biomarkers and build a nomogram. Consensus clustering defined MSRG-based subtypes, with immune profiles compared across groups. Single-cell sequencing localized key biomarkers in cardiac tissues. A transverse aortic constriction (TAC)-induced rat HF model served for in vivo validation via RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunohistochemistry. Results A total of 53 MSRG-related DEGs were identified, from which 11 core diagnostic biomarkers were selected. The nomogram model showed high predictive performance. Consensus clustering revealed two distinct HF subtypes: Cluster A exhibited enhanced metabolic and homeostatic pathways, while Cluster B showed pronounced extracellular matrix remodeling and fibrotic features, with differential immune infiltration. Single-cell analysis demonstrated CASP1 enrichment in macrophages/monocytes and PTN/MDK enrichment in fibroblasts. In vivo validation confirmed significant upregulation of PTN, MDK, and CASP1 at both mRNA and protein levels in TAC hearts, alongside elevated pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-1β) and fibrotic markers, linking mechanical stimulus-related genes to local inflammation and adverse remodeling. Conclusion MSRGs serve as robust diagnostic biomarkers for HF and enable the identification of two molecular subtypes with distinct immune microenvironment and biological pathway profiles. The CASP1-MDK-PTN axis emerges as a potential pathogenic cascade connecting mechanical stress to inflammatory and fibrotic remodeling. These findings provide a framework for early molecular subtyping, improved risk stratification, and targeted immunomodulatory therapy in HF.

papers.title: Host immunometabolic reprogramming in paediatric refractory mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia: cellular circuits, multi-omics signatures, and translational opportunities.
papers.authors: Yang J, Cui S, Li W, Liu J.
papers.abstract: Paediatric refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (RMPP) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which persistent microbial stimulation, dysregulated host immunity and evolving airway injury may coexist despite macrolide treatment. This review integrates clinical, experimental and multi-omics evidence to examine RMPP through an immunometabolic framework. Mycoplasma pneumoniae reprograms airway epithelial cells, macrophages and neutrophils by altering glycolysis, mitochondrial and redox signalling, autophagy and lipid and amino-acid metabolism. These responses can support early antimicrobial defence yet become maladaptive when inflammatory output is uncoupled from bacterial clearance. Epithelial ATP-dependent signalling, macrophage inflammasome activation, neutrophil aconitate decarboxylase 1 (ACOD1; historically termed immune-responsive gene 1 [IRG1])-itaconate activity and extracellular trap accumulation illustrate this context-dependent transition. Adaptive immune remodelling, compartment-specific Th17-regulatory T-cell imbalance and incomplete mucosal antibody protection may further sustain disease. Emerging metabolomic, lipidomic, microbiome and single-cell studies support biological heterogeneity but remain predominantly cross-sectional and cannot distinguish causal drivers from consequences of severe disease or treatment. Current mechanistic evidence is strongest for epithelial glycolysis and the neutrophil ACOD1-itaconate axis in experimental M. pneumoniae systems, whereas direct cell-resolved functional validation in paediatric RMPP remains limited, and ferroptosis and several proposed therapeutic targets remain provisional. We therefore present immunometabolic states as a hypothesis-generating framework rather than as validated endotypes. Future studies should determine whether dynamic combinations of pathogen burden, cell-specific metabolic function, inflammatory activity and anatomical injury reproducibly identify biological states that precede progression and predict differential treatment response. Longitudinal, cell-resolved studies integrating metabolic flux, pathogen trajectories, treatment exposure and anatomical evolution are required before these candidate states can support mechanism-informed clinical stratification.

papers.title: Tumor-associated macrophage reprogramming in cancer: recent advances in resistance mechanisms and therapy.
papers.authors: Saeed AF, Ashraf MN, Iqbal MZ.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant, heterogeneous, and spatially organized immune cells that regulate cancer progression, immune evasion, metastasis, and therapeutic resistance. Single-cell and spatial technologies have revealed diverse TAM states shaped by ontogeny, tumor type, disease stage, cytokines, hypoxia, metabolism, epigenetic remodeling, extracellular matrix architecture, stromal interactions, extracellular vesicles, microbiome-derived signals, and therapy-induced damage. Bidirectional cancer-TAM crosstalk evolves from tumor initiation through progression and recurrence, generating tumor-specific resistance programs that suppress lymphocytes, impair antigen presentation and phagocytosis, promote angiogenesis and metabolic restriction, remodel stroma, mediate tolerogenic efferocytosis, and sustain stem-cell, metastatic, dormancy, and regenerative niches. Therapeutic strategies include blocking macrophage recruitment or survival, activating CD40/TLR/STING signaling, targeting PI3Kγ and STAT pathways, restoring phagocytosis, modulating efferocytosis, and applying metabolic, epigenetic, stromal, vascular, nanoparticle, RNA-based, microbiome-directed, and engineered-macrophage approaches. Randomized trials have established the efficacy of CSF1R inhibition in selected CSF1-driven, macrophage-dependent tumors, whereas most other TAM- or myeloid-directed strategies in conventional solid tumors have demonstrated only preliminary clinical activity or pharmacodynamic modulation without consistent durable benefit. Off-target toxicity, spatial heterogeneity, dynamic plasticity, preclinical-clinical discordance, and combination-treatment optimization remain major barriers. Biomarker-guided patient selection, longitudinal monitoring, tumor-specific targeting, and rationally sequenced combinations will be essential for converting tumor-supportive TAMs into durable antitumor effectors.

papers.title: Immune-fibroblast ligand-receptor axes in post-infarction cardiac remodeling: convergent and divergent mechanisms compared with cancer-associated fibroblasts.
papers.authors: Lu H, Tao XL, Song DM, He YB, Zheng LZ.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction-triggered cardiac fibrosis is a cardinal feature of maladaptive ventricular remodeling and a principal contributor to heart failure pathogenesis. Enabled by single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics, accumulating evidence demonstrates that post-infarction fibrosis represents an actively coordinated biological program rather than a passive wound-healing event, which is governed by ligand-receptor-mediated crosstalk between immune cells and cardiac fibroblasts. Pioneering work has established monocyte-derived macrophages as a predominant cellular source of pro-inflammatory interleukin-1β; upon binding its cognate receptor on fibroblasts, this cytokine instigates the generation of pro-fibrotic fibroblast subsets within spatially segregated niches of the infarcted myocardium. Multiple additional ligand-receptor modules, encompassing osteopontin-CD44/integrin, transforming growth factor-β, platelet-derived growth factor, as well as growth arrest-specific protein 6-MER tyrosine kinase, further fine-tune fibroblast activation trajectories in a spatiotemporally-restricted fashion. Intriguingly, a substantial fraction of these ligand-receptor interactions are conserved in cancer-associated fibroblast biology, wherein osteopontin-producing macrophages and activated fibroblasts collaboratively build pro-tumor stromal microenvironments. We consolidate recent multi-omic findings regarding immune-fibroblast ligand-receptor communication during post-infarction cardiac remodeling, highlight mechanistic analogies to cancer-associated fibroblast activation, and discuss therapeutic prospects arising from targeting these conserved signaling nodes across cardiac and neoplastic diseases.

papers.title: Paired single-cell profiling reveals epithelial-stromal remodeling after ablative fractional carbon dioxide laser treatment in keloids.
papers.authors: Lin D, Duan L, Wang B, Chen X, Cao Y, Xu Y, Zhao S, Wang L.
papers.abstract: Background Keloids are fibroproliferative scars, but the cellular responses to ablative fractional carbon dioxide laser (AFCO2) treatment remain poorly defined. This study aimed to characterize treatment-associated epithelial, stromal and immune remodeling in patient-matched human keloid tissue. Methods We jointly reprocessed four previously reported untreated hypercellular-zone PRE specimens and four newly generated patient-matched POST specimens obtained 35 days after AFCO2 treatment from the same patients. All specimens were processed using the same Singleron Matrix/GEXSCOPE single-cell platform. Patient-aware pseudobulk differential expression, continuous transcriptional-program analysis, gene-set enrichment, trajectory and regulatory modeling, and cell-cell communication inference were integrated with independent reanalysis of GSE320017 and quantitative multiplex immunofluorescence and CD74 immunohistochemistry. The patient was the biological and inferential unit. Results After quality control, 74,937 cells were retained. A KRT6-dominant keratinocyte program increased in all four patients; KRT6B increased by 4.44 log2 units (false-discovery rate, 2.65 × 10 -5 ), with concordant increases in KRT6A and KRT16. Fibroblasts shifted toward an interferon/inflammatory program and away from a homeostatic extracellular-matrix program, whereas myeloid/APC cells showed lower HLA-DRA, C3 and MHC-II-associated antigen-presentation programs. Nine patient-supported mural-to-dendritic-cell or mural-autocrine communication axes weakened after treatment. Quantitative tissue imaging showed that CK6-family-positive area within CK14-defined epithelium increased from 2.70% to 65.84%, MMP10-positive area overlapping CK14-defined epithelium increased from 8.49% to 25.92%, and CD74-positive cell density decreased from 2,530.35 to 695.50 cells/mm². The independent hypertrophic-scar dataset showed context-dependent rather than uniform AFCO2 responses. Conclusions AFCO2 treatment was associated with coordinated epithelial, stromal and immune remodeling in human keloids, centered on a KRT6-dominant epithelial program, fibroblast-state redistribution and attenuation of an MHC-II-associated tissue context. These patient-consistent findings are exploratory and do not establish causal mechanisms.

papers.title: A conserved EREG + IL1RN + macrophage program defines an inflammation-associated transcriptional state linked to WTAP reprogramming and preterm premature rupture of membranes.
papers.authors: Zheng M, Yu Q, Zhang X, Yuan P, Liu T, Wang H.
papers.abstract: Preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM) is a major cause of spontaneous preterm birth, yet the cellular mechanisms linking inflammation to membrane dysfunction remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrated single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomic datasets from multiple maternal-fetal interface tissues to construct a comprehensive atlas of inflammatory signaling during early pregnancy. Macrophages emerged as the predominant source of basal inflammatory activity, and secondary clustering identified a conserved EREG + IL1RN + macrophages characterized by elevated inflammatory and innate immune programs. Pseudotime analysis revealed a transcriptional progression from proliferative and immunoregulatory macrophage states toward inflammatory and immune-effector states, with EREG + IL1RN + macrophages exhibiting a distinct transcriptional profile. Independent single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomic datasets confirmed the transcriptional and spatial conservation of this population. In placental infection datasets, EREG + IL1RN + macrophages were markedly expanded and enriched for cytokine signaling, leukocyte recruitment, and extracellular matrix remodeling pathways. WTAP , an m 6 A-associated candidate regulator, was positively associated with inflammatory macrophage programs, and its depletion attenuated inflammatory gene expression while promoting immunity hub-associated signatures. Clinically, the EREG + IL1RN + macrophage signature was significantly enriched in PPROM fetal membranes and showed the strongest ability to distinguish PPROM from preterm labor controls. Together, these findings identify EREG + IL1RN + macrophages as a conserved inflammatory macrophage program and implicate WTAP in inflammatory macrophage remodeling at the maternal-fetal interface.

papers.title: Inflammation- and regulated-cell-death-relevant transcriptomic signatures in bladder urothelial carcinoma: cross-cohort reproducibility, exploratory single-cell localization, and in vitro qRT-PCR validation.
papers.authors: Wang W, Zhang X, Li Z, Wang D, Cai H.
papers.abstract: Background Bladder urothelial carcinoma develops within an immune-active, metabolically stressed, and tissue-remodeling microenvironment in which regulated cell-death pathways may interact with inflammatory signaling. We evaluated whether tumor-associated transcriptional alterations are reproducible across independent cohorts and whether selected candidates can be localized at single-cell resolution and supported by in vitro expression validation. Methods TCGA-BLCA (412 primary tumors and 19 solid-tissue normal samples) and GSE13507 (165 primary tumors and 9 normal bladder mucosa controls) were analyzed independently for differential expression. A 15-gene tumor-upregulated transcriptional signature derived in TCGA was evaluated in GSE13507 without gene re-selection. Five pure-urothelial-carcinoma tumor regions from three patients in GSE293189 were analyzed exploratorily by single-cell RNA sequencing. ULBP1, IL37, COL10A1, COL11A1, and IGF2BP3 were further assessed by qRT-PCR in SV-HUC-1, T24, 5637, and UM-UC-3 cell lines. Results Across 16,759 matched genes, cohort-specific effects were positively correlated (Spearman ρ = 0.58, P -300 ), and 4,102 genes were significant in both cohorts with concordant direction. The TCGA-derived signature was higher in tumors than normal tissues and varied across reported pathologic stages, although the highly unbalanced stage distribution precluded interpretation as a clinical stage classifier. Single-cell analysis retained 1,512 cells and resolved epithelial/tumor-associated, myeloid, T-cell, B-cell, NK-cell, and fibroblast compartments with distinct basal, luminal, EMT, and immune states. All five qRT-PCR candidates were consistently upregulated in bladder-cancer cell lines relative to SV-HUC-1. Conclusion The study identifies a cross-cohort reproducible tumor-associated transcriptional signal and places selected candidates within a heterogeneous cellular context. qRT-PCR provides orthogonal expression-level support for selected candidates, but neither transcriptomic nor qRT-PCR data alone establish functional execution of apoptosis, necroptosis, pyroptosis, or ferroptosis.

papers.title: Immune microenvironment biomarkers linked to ferroptosis in clear cell renal cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Li P, Liu X, Li G.
papers.abstract: Background Clear cell renal cell carcinoma (ccRCC) is characterized by marked metabolic reprogramming and a highly heterogeneous immune microenvironment. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and has been implicated in ccRCC biology. This study aimed to identify immune-microenvironment-associated hub genes in ccRCC, examine their relationship with ferroptosis-related transcriptional changes, and evaluate their diagnostic and cellular-expression characteristics. Methods Public multi-omics data were analyzed using GSE53757 (72 ccRCC and 72 matched normal kidney tissues), GSE159115 single-cell RNA-sequencing data, and TCGA-KIRC (542 primary tumors and 72 normal kidney tissues). Differential expression, hierarchical co-expression clustering, ferroptosis-gene enrichment, protein-protein interaction analysis, MCP-counter immune scoring, single-cell localization, ROC analysis, and exploratory survival analysis were performed. In addition, in vitro qRT-PCR experiments were performed for SLC7A11, GPX4, ACSL4, and HMOX1 in RPTEC and 786-O cells and for CCR5, CSF1R, and CD86 in macrophage cultures, with three biological replicates per group, using the complete ΔCt/ΔΔCt/2 -ΔΔCt validation workflow. Results GSE53757 identified 8,650 differentially expressed genes, including significant enrichment of detected FerrDb ferroptosis genes (hypergeometric p = 2.3 × 10 -3 ). CCR5, CSF1R, CD86, CD8A, and LCP2 were significantly upregulated and clustered within the ccRCC-associated M03 immune co-expression module. MCP-counter and single-cell analyses localized these signals predominantly to macrophage and T/NK-cell compartments. TCGA-KIRC independently confirmed significant upregulation and diagnostic discrimination (AUC 0.862-0.948; five-gene panel AUC = 0.932), whereas the panel showed no independent overall-survival association. In vitro qRT-PCR measurements confirmed higher relative expression of SLC7A11, GPX4, ACSL4, and HMOX1 in 786-O than in RPTEC cells, with fold changes of 2.55, 1.58, 1.70, and 2.30, respectively; CCR5, CSF1R, and CD86 were also higher in macrophages exposed to 786-O-conditioned medium than in M0 macrophages. Conclusion CCR5, CSF1R, CD86, CD8A, and LCP2 are best interpreted as immune-microenvironment-associated hub genes in ccRCC rather than canonical ferroptosis drivers. Their association with ferroptosis is supported at the pathway and co-expression levels, while direct regulation of iron metabolism, lipid peroxidation, or the GPX4/SLC7A11 axis is not established by the present analyses. The multi-dataset evidence supports their potential diagnostic and immune-stratification value in ccRCC.

papers.title: Multi-omics integration identifies serum FTL as a novel diagnostic biomarker for esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.authors: Chen WZ, Chen SL, Han RK, Wu XR, Liang JC, Wu MT, Sun GY, Chen H.
papers.abstract: Background Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a common malignant tumor in China, with a poor five-year survival rate due to the lack of effective early diagnostic methods. This study aimed to identify potential non-invasive biomarkers and clarify their underlying mechanisms. Methods We employed an integrative approach combining serum proteomic profiling, bulk RNA sequencing, and single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) analyses. Quantitative proteomics was conducted on 15 serum samples of treatment-naive early-stage ESCC patients and 5 from healthy controls. Differentially expressed proteins (DEPs) were cross-referenced with differentially expressed genes (DEGs) from the GSE53624 dataset, and a diagnostic model was developed using LASSO regression. Cross-validation was performed using scRNA-seq data. The enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) was utilized to validate FTL in 155 serum samples from two centers. In silico FTL knockouts were conducted using scTenifoldKnk, followed by GO, KEGG, and PPI network analyses. Results Proteomic profiling identified a total of 129 DEPs. Intersection with GSE53624 DEGs yielded 8 overlapping genes, and a 6-biomarker (TF, CHAD, CSRP1, FCGR3A, RCN1, FTL) diagnostic model was built, with AUC 0.882-1.0 across validation cohorts. scRNA-seq intersection analysis identified FTL as the only overlapping DEG, exhibiting high expression levels in ESCC epithelial cells and macrophages. FTL demonstrated strong standalone diagnostic performance, with AUC values ranging from 0.872 to 0.970 across three GEO datasets. ELISA validation yielded an AUC of 0.75 (95% CI: 0.674-0.816) and 0.838 (95% CI: 0.751-0.905) for early-stage ESCC, surpassing the performance of CEA and SCCA. The combination of FTL with SCCA further enhanced discriminatory efficacy. Mechanistically, FTL was associated with altered immune cell infiltration, characterized by increased resting dendritic cells and M2 macrophages and decreased follicular helper T cells, as well as activation of the ferroptosis pathway. In silico FTL knockouts revealed DEGs enriched in stress and metabolic biological processes, extracellular vesicles (cellular component), transcriptional regulation (molecular function, CHOP-ATF3 complex), IL-17/TNF pathways, and lipid/ROS-related pathways. Protein-protein interaction hubs included FOS, ATF3, NFKBIA, and CXCL8, with FTL linked to NFE2L2, TFRC, and TXNRD1. Conclusions FTL represents a credible non-invasive serum diagnostic biomarker for ESCC. Computational analyses suggest it is a candidate molecule requiring further mechanistic and therapeutic investigation.

papers.title: A shared vascular-hypoxic transcriptional program is associated with immune organization in glioblastoma.
papers.authors: Jaskuła K, Szczepaniak A, Kugler C, Lawler SE.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) contains spatially distinct vascular and hypoxia/necrosis-associated compartments, but the extent to which these classical anatomical regions share transcriptional programs linking vascular remodeling with immune-related processes remains incompletely defined. Here, Ivy Glioblastoma Atlas Project (IvyGAP) anatomical transcriptomic data were used as a discovery framework and integrated with independent bulk and single-cell transcriptomic resources to characterize the cellular, immune and clinical context of a shared vascular-hypoxic program. Analysis of regionally defined IvyGAP compartments identified 1,114 genes enriched in vascular-associated regions and 403 genes enriched in hypoxia/necrosis-associated regions, with 95 genes shared between the two comparisons. Functional enrichment implicated angiogenesis, extracellular matrix remodeling, inflammatory signaling, chemotaxis, complement/coagulation and cytokine-related processes. The shared signature was further resolved into angiogenesis and vascular remodeling, immune and inflammatory signaling, and shared immunovascular gene subsets. Single-cell mapping showed expression of these programs across endothelial, perivascular and myeloid populations, with immune/inflammatory components also detectable in vascular-associated cell populations. Vascular remodeling genes were positively associated with inflammatory genes, stromal and exclusion scores, myeloid-enriched immune populations and immunoregulatory markers. Representative genes from each functional subset showed preferential expression in mesenchymal GBM across TCGA and CGGA, while survival modeling using the predefined combined immunovascular program separated patients into groups with distinct overall survival across three GBM cohorts. Together, these findings identify an anatomically anchored vascular-hypoxic transcriptional program associated with vascular remodeling, inflammatory signaling, immune-context features and adverse clinical outcome, providing a cross-dataset framework for interpreting immunovascular relationships in GBM.

papers.title: Spark-like T cell represents a novel functional state of CD8 + T cells associated with anti-PD-1 immunotherapy response and clinical prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Li Z, Li R, Sun F, Han C, Tian M, Song Y, Xu W, Zhang L, Huang F, Wen X, Yin X, Lin X, Tian Y.
papers.abstract: Background Spark-like T cells constitute a novel functional state of CD8 + T cells and have emerged as key drivers of immunotherapy response in preclinical models, yet their clinical relevance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains undefined. Methods Single-cell RNA sequencing (GSE207422), spatial transcriptomics (GSE271689), bulk RNA expression cohorts (TCGA-NSCLC, GSE37745, GSE41271, and GSE72094), and multiplex immunohistochemistry (mIHC) of a 100-patient cohort treated with anti-PD-1 were integrated to characterize Spark-like T cells and assess their clinical relevance. A 14-gene prognostic signature was constructed via LASSO-Cox regression. Results Spark-like T cells were significantly enriched in anti-PD-1 responders in the single-cell RNA sequencing cohort. mIHC validation in the 100-patient cohort confirmed that high Spark-like T cell intensity in tumors was independently associated with prolonged overall survival (log-rank test, p -42 ), suggesting their spatial co-enrichment with pro-inflammatory myeloid cells. In silico knockout identified TNF, ENTPD1 (CD39), and IL2 as cooperative regulators of Spark-like T cell effector function. The 14-gene Spark-like T cell-related signature (VDAC1, ITGB1, GALNT2, SEMA7A, UBB, SLC7A5, FURIN, SNX9, PSMB2, CXCL13, TOX, PPM1M, CCND2, and CLNK) robustly predicted overall survival across all four independent cohorts and remained an independent prognostic factor after adjustment for age, sex, and tumor stage. High-risk patients exhibited an immune-excluded, oncogene-driven tumor microenvironment with reduced infiltration of CD8 + T cells. Conclusions Spark-like T cells are clinically relevant determinants of anti-PD-1 response in NSCLC. mIHC quantification and the 14-gene signature provide promising translational tools for patient stratification and risk assessment.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of mast cells in mediating heart failure.
papers.authors: Zhou L, Li Y, Yue P.
papers.abstract: Cardiac mast cells have emerged as mechanistically versatile and clinically consequential mediators of heart failure and cardiomyopathy, acting through a diverse arsenal of preformed granule constituents, de novo synthesized lipid mediators, cytokines, and chemokines that collectively orchestrate myocardial injury, adverse structural remodeling, and neurohormonal dysregulation. This narrative review examines the principal molecular and cellular mechanisms through which cardiac mast cells contribute to heart failure pathogenesis, encompassing the local renin-angiotensin-aldosterone system, extracellular matrix remodeling, chemokine-mediated immune cell recruitment, preformed mediator biology, neuroimmune crosstalk, and metabolic signaling pathways. Evidence from genetic mast cell-deficiency models, pharmacological stabilization studies, transcriptomic analyses of failing human hearts, and clinical correlative investigations supports context-dependent contributions of mast cell activation to disease pathogenesis across ischemic, inflammatory, hypertensive, metabolic, and peripartum cardiomyopathy subtypes. The review further synthesizes the evidence base for mast cell-targeted therapeutic strategies-including mast cell stabilizers, chymase inhibitors, histamine receptor antagonists, neurokinin-1 receptor antagonists, and intracellular signaling modulators-and provides an integrated perspective on their potential to complement existing neurohormonal pharmacotherapy in heart failure management. Finally, emerging frontiers including single-cell transcriptomics, glyco-epigenetic regulation, right ventricular failure, and heart failure with preserved ejection fraction are discussed as priority areas for future investigation.

papers.title: Macrophage-state heterogeneity as the basis for host-directed therapy in tuberculosis.
papers.authors: Shariq M, Ehtesham NZ, Hasnain SE.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) persists partly because Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) occupies macrophages that differ in antimicrobial activity, nutrient use, inflammatory output, and drug exposure. This review examines how macrophage origin and lesion position influence phagosome maturation, responses to membrane damage, xenophagy, cytosolic sensing, regulated cell death, metabolism, and treatment response. Mtb can be taken up without lysosomal destruction, recognized by autophagy without completing lysosomal degradation, exposed to inflammatory signaling without effective killing, or retained in lesion regions with inadequate antibiotic concentrations. Evidence from single-cell studies, spatial analyses, experimental infection models, and clinical host-directed therapy studies supports evaluation of macrophage states rather than a fixed binary classification. Therapeutic candidates should be judged by linked host and bacterial outcomes, including completion of phagolysosomal or xenophagic degradation, viable bacterial burden, bacterial stress, preservation of macrophage and tissue function, lesion exposure, and compatibility with antimicrobial regimens. The evidence remains uneven: several mechanisms are well established, whereas many host-directed and nanomedicine approaches remain preclinical. Development should therefore use primary human macrophages, lesion-relevant models, lesion pharmacology, paired host-pathogen measurements, and separate microbiological, pathological, and functional endpoints. The aim is not broad immune stimulation but correction of defined macrophage and lesion states that permit persistence while preserving protective immunity.

papers.title: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) mediated gut breast crosstalk in breast cancer: integrative network analysis of molecular signaling, immune infiltration and prognostic biomarkers.
papers.authors: Aziz T, Alahmari LA, Siddig NH, Almsaud MM, Al-Asmari F, Alqahtani HA, Alonaizan R, Mengue Ngadena YS.
papers.abstract: Introduction Breast cancer is a heterogeneous malignancy in which metabolic dysregulation, immune remodelling, and complex host microbiota interactions contribute to disease progression and therapeutic response. Emerging evidence suggests that gut microbiota-derived short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), including acetate, propionate, and butyrate, may act as important molecular mediators linking the gut microbiome to systemic immune and tumor-associated signalling. However, the molecular networks through which SCFA-mediated signalling may influence breast cancer progression and the tumor immune microenvironment remains poorly characterized. This study aimed to investigate the potential regulatory mechanisms underlying the gut-breast axis by integrating SCFA host interaction networks in breast cancer transcriptomic, prognostic, immune infiltration, and drug gene interaction analyses. Methods The SCFA-host interactome was constructed from the combination of HMDB and PubChem data in a protein-protein interaction network. The identification of hub genes was conducted through topological analysis, followed by validation using TCGA-BRCA RNA-seq data, Kaplan-Meier Survival Analysis, TIMER2.0 immune analysis, and DGIdb repurposing analysis. Results The findings indicated that the genes STAT3, HIF1A, and IL6 served as key nodes connecting SCFA signalling and cancer formation. Selected SCFAs, such as propionate, have direct experimental evidence of involvement in the modulation of the JAK2/STAT3 pathway in breast cancer models, while butyrate has been associated with several breast cancer-related signalling and epigenetic mechanisms. Associations were most strongly identified in acetate which was mainly related to metabolic and immune regulatory pathways. This computational analysis did not give a quantitative ranking of the strength of interaction between SCFA and hub genes. In exploratory survival analysis without multiple-testing correction, increased STAT3 and HIF1A expression was associated with unfavourable relapse-free survival. SCFA-associated immune targets showed positive correlations with CD8+ T-cell infiltration. Discussion This study identifies the SCFA-host interactome as an essential regulatory network in breast cancer. Uncovering metabolic and signalling chokepoints such as STAT3 leads to the discovery of new biomarkers for prognosis and drug targets. This highlights the possibility of exploiting the gut-breast axis to increase immune cell penetration.

papers.title: A folate metabolism-related prognostic signature for predicting survival in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.authors: Lin L, Chen X, Wu J, Li C, Yu M, Cai B.
papers.abstract: Background Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) is highly heterogeneous, and reliable molecular prognostic biomarkers remain limited. Folate metabolism contributes to nucleotide synthesis, methyl-donor generation, and redox homeostasis, but the prognostic relevance of folate metabolism-related genes (FAMGs) in HCC remains unclear. Methods Differential expression and functional enrichment analyses of FAMGs were performed in TCGA-LIHC. A prognostic model was developed using univariate Cox and Elastic Net Cox regression and evaluated by bootstrap resampling and external validation in LIRI-JP and GSE10141. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was used for model interpretation. Immune characteristics and predicted drug responses were assessed using CIBERSORT, ssGSEA, IPS, TIDE, and oncoPredict. GSS, a candidate gene outside the model, was further examined by single-cell transcriptomic analysis and in vitro experiments. Results A total of 974 differentially expressed FAMGs were identified, and 231 prognosis-associated candidates were screened to construct a 20-gene model. The model achieved a C-index of 0.767 (95% CI, 0.718-0.815) in TCGA-LIHC and an optimism-corrected C-index of 0.676 after 999 bootstrap resamples. EPO, MYCN, PPAT, PON1, and PRDX1 showed the highest global SHAP importance. External validation showed prognostic discrimination in LIRI-JP (C-index = 0.735) but limited performance in GSE10141 (C-index = 0.495). Risk groups differed in immune-related features and predicted drug sensitivity, whereas TIDE-predicted immune checkpoint inhibitor response rates were not significantly different. Although GSS was not included in the final model, higher GSS expression was associated with poorer prognosis. Single-cell analysis showed increased GSS expression and a higher proportion of GSS-positive cells in malignant hepatocytes. In vitro , GSS knockdown inhibited Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) cell proliferation, migration, and invasion, whereas overexpression produced the opposite effects. Conclusion A 20-gene FAMG-related prognostic model was developed for HCC and showed variable performance across external cohorts, indicating that further validation is required. GSS may contribute to malignant phenotypes in HCC and warrants further mechanistic investigation.

papers.title: Bidirectional kidney-brain crosstalk in AKI, CKD, and acute brain injury: mechanisms, biomarkers, and translational perspectives.
papers.authors: Bao X, Jin R, Zhang L, Pan L, Jiang F.
papers.abstract: The kidney and brain share vascular, metabolic, immune, and neuroendocrine pathways through which dysfunction in either organ can affect the other. Acute kidney injury is associated with delirium and encephalopathy, whereas chronic kidney disease contributes to a longer-term burden of cognitive and cerebrovascular impairment. Retained solutes, drug accumulation, endothelial injury, and systemic inflammation can disrupt the blood-brain barrier and alter glial and neuronal function. Recent experimental studies identify microglial potassium efflux, inflammasome activation, gasdermin D signaling, and ferroptotic stress as components of these responses. Changes in Klotho-FGF23 signaling and impaired perivascular brain clearance provide additional links between renal dysfunction and neurological vulnerability. In the reverse direction, kidney injury after acute brain injury reflects overlapping brain-driven responses, secondary systemic or treatment-related insults, and pre-existing renal and vascular susceptibility. This narrative review brings these mechanisms together with clinical observations and findings from proteomics, metabolomics, and single-cell transcriptomics. It also examines how kidney function affects circulating neurological biomarkers and how study design influences their interpretation. Established management focuses on reversible metabolic disturbances, renal and cerebral perfusion, and medication-related risk. Experimental interventions are discussed according to the disease models and outcomes studied, with emphasis on the evidence needed to translate molecular targets into improvements in cognition, neurological recovery, and kidney function.

papers.title: A single-cell atlas of the human respiratory system identifies a monocyte-centered HSPA1B + inflammatory primed state associated with WTAP.
papers.authors: Wang Y, Zhu L, Zhu Y, Chen G.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent pulmonary inflammation and tissue remodeling, yet the cellular states and regulatory mechanisms underlying monocyte functional heterogeneity remain incompletely understood. Here, we generate a high-resolution single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the human respiratory system and identify a diverse monocyte functional landscape in healthy lungs containing a HSPA1B + inflammatory monocytes state. This population exhibits enhanced inflammatory programs, cytokine and chemokine activity, and shows a distinct position within the inferred transcriptional landscape of the continuous monocyte functional spectrum. Cell-cell communication analysis further reveals that HSPA1B + inflammatory monocytes function as active communication nodes within a stromal-immune-vascular network, integrating MIF, extracellular matrix, and immune-regulatory signals while mediating CXCL and adhesion-associated interactions with surrounding cellular compartments. Comparative analysis of COPD lung tissues and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid demonstrates selective enrichment of this inflammatory monocyte program in disease-associated environments, whereas peripheral blood monocytes from healthy individuals and COPD patients show limited representation of this state. Integrated transcriptomic and m 6 A regulator-associated analyses identify WTAP, a core component of the m 6 A methyltransferase complex, as a factor associated with the inflammatory monocytes program. WTAP silencing in inflammatory monocyte models suppresses pro-inflammatory mediators while enhancing interferon-response and antigen-presentation programs. Collectively, these findings define an inflammatory monocyte state landscape in the human respiratory system and identify a WTAP-associated transcriptional program linked to monocyte inflammatory activation and functional remodeling in COPD. This study provides new insights into the organization of pulmonary immune states and the potential regulatory mechanisms underlying chronic inflammatory regulation in COPD.

papers.title: Hypoxia-driven macrophage heterogeneity in sepsis: single-cell transcriptomic insights into immune reprogramming and therapeutic targeting.
papers.authors: Yu Y, Wang Z, Li Y, Jing C, Li X.
papers.abstract: Sepsis is characterized by profound immune dysregulation and metabolic remodeling, yet how hypoxia shapes macrophage-state diversity remains incompletely defined. Here, we integrated single-cell transcriptomic profiles from early- and late-stage sepsis with healthy controls to construct a hypoxia-centered immune atlas. The single-cell landscape identified 103,851 cells across 23 clusters, while hypoxia scoring showed that macrophages displayed the strongest hypoxic activity, particularly in early sepsis. Macrophages were further stratified into low-, intermediate- and high-hypoxic states, revealing a continuous transcriptional gradient rather than discrete subsets. High-hypoxic macrophages exhibited increased CytoTRACE-defined plasticity, occupied intermediate-to-late pseudotime states, and showed enhanced inflammatory and metabolic pathway activation. Cell-cell communication analysis positioned these macrophages as bidirectional signaling hubs, with amplified MIF, CCL, ANNEXIN and IL1-related interactions. Integrated high dimensional Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (hdWGCNA) and machine-learning analyses identified hypoxia-associated hub genes, among which TIPARP emerged as a key regulator linked to macrophage hypoxic remodeling. TIPARP was preferentially enriched in high-hypoxic macrophages and experimentally validated as responsive to hypoxia and inflammatory stimulation, with knockdown can enhance HIF1A and VEGF induction. Drug-sensitivity prediction further suggested state-specific vulnerabilities of hypoxia-adapted macrophages. Together, these findings define hypoxia as a central determinant of macrophage heterogeneity in sepsis and nominate TIPARP as a candidate target for immunometabolic intervention.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights and translational perspectives on liver fibrosis through single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.authors: Lu W, Xu J, Wang K, Chen Y, Cherubini A, Valenti L, Zheng S, Liu Z.
papers.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a defining feature of chronic liver diseases and can progress to cirrhosis and liver failure. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables high-resolution analysis of cellular heterogeneity and multicellular interactions during fibrogenesis. In this narrative review, we analyzed published single-cell transcriptomic studies from experimental models and human cohorts, focusing on cell-type-specific programs, cell-state trajectories inferred by Monocle, and intercellular communication networks predicted using CellChat and CellPhoneDB. Hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) consistently emerged as the primary extracellular matrix-producing cells, with conserved activation signatures involving collagen synthesis, Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase-Protein kinase B (PI3K-AKT) signaling, and matrix organization. Macrophage analyses identified fibrosis-associated subsets, including CD9 + and TREM2 + scar-associated macrophages (SAMs), which regulate inflammation, angiogenesis, and stromal remodeling. Liver sinusoidal endothelial cells undergo capillarization and transcriptional reprogramming linked to WNT signaling and antigen presentation. B cells exhibit activation signatures related to B-cell receptor signaling. Trajectory analyses infer potential cell-state transitions based on transcriptional similarity from quiescent to pathogenic states, including stepwise HSC activation and monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation. Cell-cell communication analysis highlights HSC-macrophage interactions, with key axes such as predicted Chemokine ligand 2-chemokine receptor 2 (CCL2-CCR2) and transforming growth factor-β-transforming growth factor-β receptor (TGFβ-TGFβR) signaling interactions that may contribute to fibrogenic communication networks. These findings define conserved multicellular programs and support integrated multi-omics approaches for biomarker discovery and therapy.

papers.title: T-BET promotes inflammatory specialization without driving terminal maturation of iPSC-derived NK cells.
papers.authors: Marsal C, Kashif M, Borate S, Hållstrand C, Haazen L, Gilljam M, Dölalan Y, Burduli N, Meinke S, Norman A, Hussain A, Lanner F, Sitnicka E, Alici E.
papers.abstract: Induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs) provide a scalable platform for off-the-shelf immune cell therapies; however, the mechanisms controlling maturation and functional specialization of iPSC-derived natural killer (iNK) cells are not fully understood. In this study, we combined single-cell transcriptomics, phenotypic profiling, and functional assays to characterize iNK cells and to determine whether temporally controlled expression of the transcription factor T-BET (TBX21) can promote iNK terminal specification and effector functions. Single-cell RNA sequencing and phenotypic profiling confirmed that baseline iNK cells form a transcriptionally distinct NK population and retain a developmental transcriptional signature. These iNK cells exhibited incomplete terminal maturation compared with peripheral blood NK cells, expressing much of the cytotoxic machinery but displaying limited acquisition of maturation-associated receptors. Despite induction of selected terminal specification markers, T-BET did not shift iNK cells toward a peripheral NK-like transcriptional identity. Instead, T-BET selectively triggered an inflammatory effector program characterized by elevated CCL3 , CCL5 and GZMA expression and increased IFNγ production across multiple tumor targets, without enhancement of terminal cytotoxic gene programs. These findings suggest a functional dissociation between inflammatory and cytotoxic programs in iPSC-derived NK cells. This work highlights transcriptional engineering as a strategy to modulate functional state in stem cell-derived NK cells.

papers.title: Trans-MMVAE: A transformer-based multi-modal variational autoencoder for interpretable multi-omics target prioritization in allergic rhinitis.
papers.authors: Wang Q, Sui X, Cui S, Zhang X, Song W.
papers.abstract: BackgroundAllergic rhinitis (AR) presents a highly heterogeneous multi-omics landscape, necessitating advanced computational frameworks to uncover underlying disease mechanisms and facilitate precise clinical interventions. Conventional deep learning approaches often lack the biological context required for translational application.MethodsWe propose Trans-MMVAE, a transformer-based multi-modal variational autoencoder engineered specifically as an interpretable computational framework for multi-omics target discovery rather than a general data mining tool. Our architecture directly integrates heterogeneous clinical and multi-omics data. By utilizing a specialized Regression Head, the framework maps high-dimensional latent space representations directly to clinical scores, effectively bridging the gap between molecular profiles and phenotypic severity.ResultsUpon rigorous evaluation with real-world AR cohorts, Trans-MMVAE accurately recaptured canonical lipid metabolism targets, particularly ALOX15 and ALOX5. Serving as robust biological positive controls, these identifications validated the model's capacity to isolate true functional signals from severe multi-omics noise. Crucially, the framework expanded the interactome of these known targets by delineating the multi-layered metabolic-immune crosstalk linking lipid metabolism and the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway in the context of AR. Through integrated cross-modal scoring, the model systematically prioritized KMO and HAAO-enzymes in the kynurenine pathway previously implicated in broader allergic inflammation-and positioned them as potential mechanistic bridges between lipid dysregulation and Th2 immune activation in AR specifically. Epithelial-derived cytokines TSLP and IL33 were concurrently identified as synergistic downstream nodes within this integrated network.ConclusionBy shifting the paradigm from single-target rediscovery to systemic multi-omics landscape mapping, Trans-MMVAE demonstrates consistent performance across cross-validation folds and an independent external cohort. It establishes a systematic computational methodology for multi-modal data integration that generates testable mechanistic hypotheses regarding metabolic-immune crosstalk in AR, which require validation in larger, multi-center studies.
